body.translated_text: <s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> (The Array of the Land of Bliss) / [Extended Version]

body.text: om namo ratnatrayāya | om namaḥ śrīsarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | namo daśadiganantāparyantalokadhātupratiṣṭhitebhyaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvāryaśrāvakapratyekabuddhebhyo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannebhyaḥ | namo 'mitābhāya | namo 'cintyaguṇāntarātmane ||
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the Three Jewels. <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to all the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Homage to all the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, noble <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples), and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) established in the world-realms of the ten directions, infinite and boundless — past, future, and present. Homage to <s>Amitābha</s> (Infinite Light). Homage to him whose inner nature is of inconceivable qualities.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭaparvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ dvātriṃśatā bhikṣusahasraiḥ, sarvairarhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravairniḥkleśairuṣitavadbhiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ parīkṣacittaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanairanuprāptasvakārthairvijitavadbhiruttamadamathaprāptaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñairmahānāgaiḥ ṣaḍabhijñairvaśībhūtairaṣṭavimokṣadhyāyibhirbalaprāptairabhijñātābhijñaiḥ sthavirairmahāśrāvakaiḥ | tadyathā - ājñātakauṇḍinyena ca, aśvajitā ca,bāṣpeṇa ca,mahānāmnā ca, bhadrajitā ca, yaśodevena ca, vimalena ca,subāhunā ca, pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputreṇa ca, urubilvākāśyapena ca, nadīkāśyapena ca, gayākāśyapena ca, kumārakāśyapena ca, mahākāśyapena ca, śāriputreṇa ca, mahāmaudgalyāyanena ca, mahākauṣṭhilyena ca, mahākaphilena ca, mahācundena ca, aniruddhena ca, nandikena ca, kampilena ca, subhūtinā ca, revatena ca, khadiravanikena ca, vakulena ca, svāgatena ca, amogharājena ca, pārāyaṇikena ca, patkena ca, cullapatkena ca, nandena ca,rāhulena ca,āyuṣmatānandena ca,etaiścānyaiśca abhijñātābhijñaiḥ sthavirairmahāśrāvakairekaṃ pudgalaṃ sthāpayitvā śaikṣapratidyuttarikaraṇīyaṃ yadidamāyuṣmantamānandam | maitreyapūrvaṃgamaiśca saṃbahulairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ || Sukhv_1 ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of monks, thirty-two thousand monks in all — all of them <s>Arhats</s> (worthy ones) whose defilements were exhausted, free from afflictions, who had lived well, whose minds were well-liberated through right knowledge, whose minds were thoroughly examined, whose bonds of existence were exhausted, who had accomplished their own purpose, who had conquered like conquerors, who had attained the supreme taming, who were well-liberated in mind, well-liberated in wisdom, great <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings, i.e., noble ones), who had attained the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), who had gained mastery, who meditated on the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), who had attained power, well-known and distinguished — the elder great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples). Namely: <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, <s>Aśvajit</s>, <s>Bāṣpa</s>, <s>Mahānāman</s>, <s>Bhadrajit</s>, <s>Yaśodeva</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, <s>Nadīkāśyapa</s>, <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>, <s>Kumārakāśyapa</s>, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Mahākauṣṭhilya</s>, <s>Mahākapphila</s>, <s>Mahācunda</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Nandika</s>, <s>Kampila</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Revata</s>, <s>Khadiravanika</s>, <s>Vakula</s>, <s>Svāgata</s>, <s>Amogharāja</s>, <s>Pārāyaṇika</s>, <s>Patka</s>, <s>Cullapatka</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Rāhula</s>, and the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> — together with these and other well-known and distinguished elder great disciples, excepting one individual who was still a learner with something further to accomplish, namely the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>; and together with a great multitude of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings), led by <s>Maitreya</s>.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānda utthāyāsamādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - viprasannāni tava bhagavata indriyāṇi, pariśuddhaśchavivarṇaḥ, paryavadāto mukhavarṇaḥ pītanirbhāsaḥ | tadyathāpi nāma śāradaṃ vanadaṃ pāṇḍupariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ pītanirbhāsam, evameva bhagavato viprasannānīndriyāṇi, pariśuddho mukhavarṇaḥ, paryavadātaśchavivarṇaḥ pītanirbhāsaḥ | tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan jāmbūnadasuvarṇaniṣko dakṣeṇa karmāreṇa karmārāntevāsinā vā ulkāmukhena saṃpraveśya supariniṣṭhitaḥ (
Sukhv, Vaidya 222
children.translated_text: [Sukhv, Vaidya p. 222]

children.text: ) pāṇḍukambala uparinikṣipto 'tīva pariśuddho bhavati paryavadātaḥ pītanirbhāsaḥ, evameva bhagavato ciprasannānīndriyāṇi, pariśuddho mukhavarṇaḥ, paryavadātaśchavivarṇaḥ pītanirbhāsaḥ | na khalu punarahaṃ bhagavan abhijānāmi itaḥ pūrvataramevaṃ viprasannāni tathāgatasyendriyāṇi evaṃ poariśuddhaṃ mukhavarṇaṃ paryavadātaṃ chavivarṇaṃ pītanirbhāsam | tasya me bhagavan evaṃ bhavati - buddhavihāreṇa batādya tathāgato vihārati, jinavihāreṇa sarvajñatāvihāeṇa | mahānāgavihāreṇa batādya tathāgato viharati | atītānāgatapratyutpannān vā tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān samanusmaratīti | evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - sādhu sādhvānanda | kiṃ punaste devatā etamarthamārocayanti, utāho buddhā bhagavntaḥ? atha tena pratyutpannamīmāṃsājñānenaivaṃ prajānāsīti? evamukte āyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - na me bhagavan devatā etamarthamārocayanti, nāpi buddhā bhagavantaḥ | atha tarhi me bhagavaṃstenaiva pratyātmamīmāṃsājñānenaivaṃ bhavati - buddhavihāreṇādya tathāgato viharati | jinavihāreṇa sarvajñatāvihāreṇa batādya tathāgato viharati | atītānāgatapratyutpannān vā buddhān bhagavataḥ samanusmaratīti | evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - sādhu sādhvānanda | udāraḥ khalu te unmiñjaḥ,bhadrikā mīmāṃsā,kalyāṇaṃ pratibhānam | bahujanahitāya tvamānanda pratipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyayārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca, yastvaṃ tathāgatamarthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase | evameva bhagavatsu ānandastathāgateṣvarhatsu samyaksaṃbuddheṣu aprameyeṣu asaṃkhyeyeṣu jñānadarśanamupasaṃharet, na tathāgatasya jñānamupahanyeta | tatkasya hetoḥ? apratihatahetujñānadarśano hyānanda tathāgataḥ | jñānamākāṅkṣannānanda tathāgataḥ ekapiṇḍapātena kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpaśataṃ vā kalpaśatasahasraṃ vā yāvatkalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraṃ vā, tato vottari tiṣṭhet, na ca tathāgatasyendriyāṇyupanaśyeyuḥ, na mukhavarṇasyānyathātvaṃ bhavet, nāpi cchavivarṇa upahanyeta | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi ānanda tathāgataḥ samādhimukhapāramitāprāptaḥ | samyaksaṃbuddhānāmānanda loke sudurlabhaḥ prādurbhāvaḥ | tadyathā audumbarapuṣpāṇāṃ loke prādurbhāvaḥ sudurlabho bhavati, evameva ānanda tathāgatānāmarthakāmānāṃ hitaiṣīṇāmanukampakānāṃ mahākaruṇāpratipannānāṃ sudurlabhaḥ prādurbhāvaḥ | api tu khalvānanda tathāgatasyaiva so 'nubhāvo yastvaṃ sarvalokācāryāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ loke prādurbhāvāya bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmarthāya tathāgatametamarthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase | tena hyānanda śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru | bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te | evaṃ bhagavan ityāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt || Sukhv_2 ||
children.translated_text: and placed upon a pale-yellow cloth, becomes exceedingly pure, clear, and shining with a golden glow — even so, Blessed One, your faculties are serene, your facial color is pure, your complexion is clear and shining with a golden glow. Never before, Blessed One, have I known the <s>Tathāgata's</s> (Thus-Gone One's) faculties to be so serene, his facial color so pure, his complexion so clear and shining with a golden glow. This thought occurred to me, Blessed One: 'Surely today the <s>Tathāgata</s> abides in the abiding of a <s>Buddha</s>, the abiding of a conqueror, the abiding in omniscience. Surely today the <s>Tathāgata</s> abides in the abiding of a great <s>nāga</s>. Perhaps he is recollecting the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones of past, future, and present.' " When this was said, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> thus: "Excellent, excellent, <s>Ānanda</s>! Did the gods inform you of this matter, or the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones? Or do you know this by your own present investigation and insight?" When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: "Neither the gods, Blessed One, have informed me of this matter, nor the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. Rather, Blessed One, by my own personal investigation and insight, this thought occurred to me: 'Today the <s>Tathāgata</s> abides in the abiding of a <s>Buddha</s>, the abiding of a conqueror, the abiding in omniscience. Surely today the <s>Tathāgata</s> abides in the abiding of a great <s>nāga</s>. Perhaps he is recollecting the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones of past, future, and present.' " When this was said, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> thus: "Excellent, excellent, <s>Ānanda</s>! Noble indeed is your inference, auspicious your investigation, excellent your inspired understanding. You, <s>Ānanda</s>, have set forth for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the sake, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, of gods and humans — you who think to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about this matter. Even so, <s>Ānanda</s>, even if one were to bring knowledge and vision to bear upon immeasurable, incalculable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened Blessed Ones, the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> would not be diminished. For what reason? Because, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision of causes is unobstructed. If the <s>Tathāgata</s> so wished, <s>Ānanda</s>, he could live on a single alms-meal for a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), or a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, or a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, or even up to a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>niyutas</s> (billions) of <s>kalpas</s>, or even beyond that, and the <s>Tathāgata's</s> faculties would not diminish, nor would there be any change in his facial color, nor would his complexion be impaired. For what reason? Because, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has attained the perfection of the entrance into <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption). The appearance of perfectly and fully awakened ones in the world, <s>Ānanda</s>, is extremely rare — just as the appearance of <s>udumbara</s> (fig-tree) flowers in the world is extremely rare, even so, <s>Ānanda</s>, the appearance of <s>Tathāgatas</s> who desire the welfare, who seek the benefit, who are compassionate, who have entered upon great compassion — their appearance is extremely rare. However, <s>Ānanda</s>, it is by the very power of the <s>Tathāgata</s> that you think to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about this matter, for the sake of the appearance in the world of all beings who are teachers of the world, for the benefit of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings). Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, listen well and carefully attend. I shall speak to you." "Yes, Blessed One," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the Blessed One.

Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the Blessed One, he addressed the Blessed One thus: "Your faculties, O Blessed One, are serene; your complexion is pure; your facial color is clear and shining with a golden glow. Just as an autumn lotus, pale-white and pure, clear and shining with a golden glow — even so, Blessed One, your faculties are serene, your facial color is pure, your complexion is clear and shining with a golden glow. Just as, Blessed One, a nugget of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, when a skilled goldsmith or goldsmith's apprentice inserts it into the furnace-mouth and it is thoroughly refined,

After <s>Siṃhamati</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, far beyond, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully awakened one named <s>Lokeśvararāja</s> — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. In the teaching of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully awakened one, <s>Ānanda</s>, there was a monk named <s>Dharmākara</s> — exceedingly endowed with mindfulness, intelligence, understanding, and wisdom, exceedingly endowed with vigor, and of noble aspiration.

The Blessed One addressed <s>Ānanda</s> thus: "In the past, <s>Ānanda</s>, in a former age, in a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) incalculable, more incalculable still, vast, immeasurable, and inconceivable ago — at that time, in that period, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully awakened one named <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>. After <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, far beyond, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Pratāpavān</s>. After him, far beyond, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Prabhākara</s>. After him, far beyond, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Candanagandha</s>. After him, far beyond, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sumerukalpa</s>.

children.text: START Sukhv 4:
children.translated_text: [Section 4:]

children.text: atha khalvānanda sa dharmākaro bhikṣurutthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yenāsau bhagavāṃllokeśvararājastathāgatastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantaṃ namaskṛtya tasminneva samaye saṃmukhamābhirgāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt -
children.translated_text: Then, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Dharmākara</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>, he bowed to the Blessed One and at that very time praised him face to face with these verses:

children.text: amitaprabha anantatulyabuddhe na ca iha anya prabhā vibhāti kācit /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Buddha</s> of infinite radiance, equal to the boundless — no other light shines here at all;

children.text: sūryamaṇigirīśacandraābhā na tapita bhosiṣu ebhi sarvaloke // Sukhv_vs_1 //
children.translated_text: the radiance of the sun, of jewels, of the lord of mountains, and of the moon does not blaze in all the worlds compared to these.

children.text: rūpamapi anantu attvasāre tatha api buddhasvaro anantaghoṣaḥ /
Sukhv, Vaidya 224
śīlamapi samādhiprajñavīryaiḥ sadṛśu na te 'stiha loki kaścidanyaḥ // Sukhv_vs_2 //
children.translated_text: in morality, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), wisdom, and vigor, there is no one else like you in this world.
Your form too is infinite, without compare, and so too the voice of the <s>Buddha</s> is of infinite sound;

children.text: gabhiru vipulu sūkṣmaprāptu dharmo 'cintitu buddhavaro yathā samudraḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) is deep, vast, subtle, and attained — inconceivable, like the ocean, is this supreme <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: tenonnamanā na cāsti śāstuḥ khiladoṣān jahyā ato 'dhikālam // Sukhv_vs_3 //
children.translated_text: therefore there is no measurement of the Teacher — may I abandon all faults and defilements henceforth.

children.text: atha buddhabalā anantatejā pratapati sarvadiśā narendrarājā /
children.translated_text: Then, with the infinite splendor of the <s>Buddha's</s> powers, the king among the best of men shines in all directions;

children.text: tatha ahu buddha bhavi dharmasvāmī jaramaraṇātprajāṃ pramocayeyam // Sukhv_vs_4 //
children.translated_text: thus I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, a lord of the <s>Dharma</s>, and I shall liberate beings from old age and death.

children.text: dānaśamathaśīlakṣāntivīrya dhyānasamādhitaścaiva agraśreṣṭhāṃ /
children.translated_text: Generosity, tranquility, morality, patience, vigor, <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — the foremost and supreme of these;

children.text: ebhi ahu vratāṃ samādadāmi buddha bhaviṣyami sarvasattvatrātā // Sukhv_vs_5 //
children.translated_text: these vows I shall undertake — I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, the protector of all beings.

children.text: buddhaśatasahasra koṭyanekā yathariva vālika gaṅgayā anantā /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s>, as innumerable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: sarvata ahu pūjayiṣya nāthāṃ śivavarabodhigaveṣako atulyāṃ // Sukhv_vs_6 //
children.translated_text: I shall worship all the Protectors everywhere, the incomparable seekers of the supreme, auspicious <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening).

children.text: gaṅgārajasamānalokadhātūṃ tatra bhūyo 'ntari ye anantakṣetrāḥ /
children.translated_text: In world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and further still, the infinite fields within them;

children.text: sarvatra prabha muñcayiṣya tatrā iti etādṛśa vīryamārabhidhya // Sukhv_vs_7 //
children.translated_text: everywhere I shall release my radiance therein — with such vigor shall I strive.

children.text: kṣetra mama udāru agra śreṣṭho varamiha malī(?) saṃskṛte 'smiṃ /
children.translated_text: My <s>kṣetra</s> (buddha-field) shall be noble, supreme, the finest — incomparable in this conditioned world;

children.text: asadṛśa nirvāṇadhātusaukhyaṃ taśca(cca?) asattvatayā viśodhayiṣye // Sukhv_vs_8 //
children.translated_text: with the bliss of the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> realm, unequaled, I shall purify it of all impurity.

children.text: daśadiśata samāgatāni sattvāḥ tatra gatā sukha me diśanti kṣipram /
children.translated_text: Beings coming from the ten directions, having gone there, shall quickly receive happiness from me;

children.text: buddha mama pramāṇu atra śikṣī avitathavīryabalaṃ janemi chandam // Sukhv_vs_9 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddha</s> is my measure, here is my training — I shall generate the aspiration with the power of unfailing vigor.

children.text: daśadiśalokavidasaṅgajñānī sada mama citta prajānayanti te 'pi /
children.translated_text: The knowers of the world in the ten directions, of unattached wisdom — may they always know my mind as well;

children.text: avicigatu ahaṃ sadā vaseyaṃ praṇidhibalaṃ na punarvivartayiṣye // Sukhv_vs_10 //
children.translated_text: I shall always dwell even in the <s>Avīci</s> hell — by the power of my vow I shall never turn back.

children.text: || Sukhv_4 ||
START Sukhv 5:
children.translated_text: [Section 5:]

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 225

atha khalvānanda sa dharmākaro bhikṣustaṃ bhagavantaṃ lokeśvararājaṃ tathāgataṃ saṃmukhamābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya etadavocat - ahamasmi bhagavan uttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmaḥ | punaḥ punaranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayāmi pariṇāmayāmi | tasya me bhagavān śāstā tathā dharmaṃ deśayatu, yathāhaṃ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam | asamasamastathāgato loke bhaveyam | tāṃśca bhagavānākārān parikīrtayatu yairahaṃ buddhakṣetrasya guṇavyūhasaṃpadaṃ parigṛhṇīyām | evamukte ānanda bhagavāṃllokeśvararājastathāgatastaṃ bhikṣumetadavocat - tena hi tvaṃ bhikṣo svayameva buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadaṃ parigṛhṇīṣva | so 'vocat - nāhaṃ bhagavaṃstatsaheyam, api tu bhagavāneva | bhāṣasva anyeṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhālaṃkārasaṃpadam, yāṃ śrutvā vayaṃ sarvākāraṃ paripūrayiṣyāma iti | athānanda sa lokeśvararājastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastasya bhikṣurāśayaṃ jñātvā paripūrṇāṃ varṣakoṭīmekāśītibuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadaṃ sākārāṃ soddeśāṃ sanirdeśāṃ saṃprakāśitavānarthakāmo hitaiṣī anukampako 'nukampāmupādāya buddhakṣetrānupacchedāya sattveṣu mahākaruṇāṃ saṃjanayitvā | paripūrṇāścatvāriṃśatkalpāstasya bhagavatastathāgatasyāyuḥpramāṇam || Sukhv_5 ||
children.translated_text: Then, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Dharmākara</s>, having praised that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>, face to face with these verses, spoke thus: "I, Blessed One, wish to awaken to the supreme, perfect <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening). Again and again I generate and dedicate the mind to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening. May the Blessed One, as my teacher, so teach me the <s>Dharma</s> that I may quickly awaken to the supreme, perfect awakening. May I become a <s>Tathāgata</s> unequaled and without equal in the world. And may the Blessed One describe those qualities by which I may comprehend the perfected array of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field)." When this was said, <s>Ānanda</s>, the Blessed One <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, addressed that monk thus: "Then you, monk, should yourself comprehend the perfected array of adornments and qualities of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>." He replied: "I am not capable of that, Blessed One. Rather, may the Blessed One himself describe the perfected array of adornments and qualities of the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> of other <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Having heard it, we shall fulfill it in every respect." Then, <s>Ānanda</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully awakened one, knowing the aspiration of that monk, for a full eighty-one hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, illuminated the perfected array of adornments and qualities of their <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in detail, with its aspects, its outlines, and its explanations — desiring their welfare, seeking their benefit, compassionate, out of compassion, for the sake of the continuity of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, having generated great compassion toward beings. The lifespan of that Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> was a full forty <s>kalpas</s> (aeons).

children.text: START Sukhv 6:
children.translated_text: [Section 6:]

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 226

atha khalvānanda sa dharmākaro bhikṣuryāsteṣāmekāśītibuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadaḥ, tāḥ sarvā eke buddhakṣetre parigṛhya bhagavato lokeśvararājasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvā pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tasya bhagavato 'ntikātprākrāmat | uttari ca pañca kalpān buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadamudāratarāṃ praṇītatarāṃ ca sarvaloke daśasu dikṣu apracaritapūrvāṃ parigṛhītavān, udārataraṃ ca praṇidhānamakārṣīt || Sukhv_6 ||
children.translated_text: Then, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Dharmākara</s>, having comprehended in one <s>buddhakṣetra</s> all the perfected arrays of adornments and qualities of those eighty-one hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, circumambulated him, and departed from the presence of that Blessed One. For a further five <s>kalpas</s>, he comprehended the perfected array of adornments and qualities of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> — more noble and more excellent than any previously known in the world in the ten directions — and he made a most noble vow.

children.text: START Sukhv 7:
children.translated_text: [Section 7:]

children.text: iti hyānanda yā tena bhagavatā lokeśvararājena tathāgatena teṣāmekāśītibuddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ saṃpattiḥ kathitā, tato bhikṣurekāśītyudārapraṇītāprameyatarāṃ buddhakṣetrasaṃpattiṃ parigṛhya yena sa tathāgatastenopasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā etadavocat - parigṛhītā me bhagavan buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpaditi | evamukte ānanda sa lokeśvararājastathāgatastaṃ bhikṣumetadavocat - tena hi bhikṣo bhāṣasva, anumodate tathāgataḥ | ayaṃ kālo bhikṣo, pramodaya parṣadam, harṣaṃ janaya, siṃhanādaṃ nada,yaṃ śrutvā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā etarhyanāgate 'dhvani evaṃrūpāṇi buddhakṣetraguṇasaṃpattipraṇidhisthānāni parigrahīṣyanti | athānanda sa dharmākaro bhikṣustasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavantametadavocat - tena hi śṛṇotu me bhagavān ye mama praṇidhānaviśeṣāḥ, yathā me 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya acintyaguṇālaṃkāravyūhasamanvāgataṃ tad buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati || Sukhv_7 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, the perfection of those eighty-one hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> was described by that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>. Then the monk, having comprehended a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> perfection eighty-one times more noble, more excellent, and more immeasurable, approached that <s>Tathāgata</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and spoke thus: "I have comprehended, Blessed One, the perfected array of adornments and qualities of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>." When this was said, <s>Ānanda</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s> addressed that monk thus: "Then, monk, speak. The <s>Tathāgata</s> approves. This is the time, monk — gladden the assembly, generate joy, roar the lion's roar, hearing which <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings) in the future shall comprehend the stations of vows for such <s>buddhakṣetra</s> perfections of qualities." Then, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Dharmākara</s> at that moment addressed the Blessed One thus: "Then let the Blessed One hear my specific vows — by which, when I have awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening, that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall be endowed with an array of inconceivable adornments and qualities."

children.text: START Sukhv 8:
children.translated_text: [Section 8:]

children.text: 1. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre nirayo vā tiryagyonirvā pretaviṣayo vā āsuro vā kāyo bhavet, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: "1. If, Blessed One, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of mine there should be a hell, or an animal realm, or a realm of hungry ghosts, or a body of <s>asuras</s> (titans), then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 2. sacenme bhagavaṃstasya tatra buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājātā bhaveyuḥ, te punastataścyutvā nirayaṃ vā tiryagyoniṃ vā pretaviṣayaṃ vā āsuraṃ vā kāyaṃ prapateyuḥ,mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 2. If, Blessed One, those beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of mine, having fallen from there, should fall into a hell, an animal realm, a realm of hungry ghosts, or a body of <s>asuras</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 3. sacenme bhagavaṃstatra buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājātāste ca sarve naikavarṇāḥ syuryadidaṃ suvarṇavarṇāḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 3. If, Blessed One, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, the beings who are reborn there should not all be of one color, namely the color of gold, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 4. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca nānātvaṃ prajñāyeta anyatra nāma saṃvṛtivyavahāramātrā devamanuṣyā iti saṃkhyāgaṇanātaḥ,mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 4. If, Blessed One, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, any difference between gods and humans should be discerned, except for the mere conventional designation 'gods and humans' as a matter of counting and naming, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 5. sacenme bhagavaṃtasmin buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ, te ca sarve na ṛddhivaśitāparamapāramitāprāptā bhaveyuḥ, antaśa ekacittakṣaṇalavena buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrātikramaṇatayāpi, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 5. If, Blessed One, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all attain the supreme perfection of mastery over supernatural powers, including the ability to traverse a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in a single mind-moment, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 6. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājātā bhaveyuḥ, te ca sarve jātismarā na syuḥ, antaśaḥ kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrānusmaraṇatayāpi, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 6. If, Blessed One, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all possess the memory of past lives, including the ability to remember a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 7. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājāyeran, te sarve na divyasya cakṣuṣo lābhino bhaveyuḥ, antaśo lokadhātukoṭīniyutaśatasahasradarśanatayāpi, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 7. If, Blessed One, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all gain the divine eye, including the ability to see a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of world-realms, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 8. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājāyeran, te sarve na divyasya śrotrasya lābhino bhaveyuḥ, antaśo buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrādapi yugapatsaddharmaśravaṇatayā, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 8. If, Blessed One, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all gain the divine ear, including the ability to hear the true <s>Dharma</s> simultaneously from a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 9. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājāyeran, te sarve na paracittajñānakovidā bhaveyuḥ, antaśo buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparyāpannānāmapi sattvānāṃ cittacaritaparijñānatayā, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 9. If, Blessed One, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all become skilled in the knowledge of others' minds, including the ability to know the mental conduct of all beings contained within a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 10. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājāyeran, teṣāṃ kācitparigrahasaṃjñotpadyeta, antaśaḥ svaśarīre 'pi, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 10. If, Blessed One, among the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, any notion of possessiveness should arise, even regarding their own bodies, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 11. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājāyeran, te sarve na niyatāḥ syuryādidaṃ samyaktve yāvanmahāparinirvāṇe, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 11. If, Blessed One, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all be assured of the right course, up to and including the great <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation), then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 12. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya kaścitsattvaḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ gaṇanāmadhigacchet, antaśastrisāhasramahāsāhasraparyāpannā api sarvasattvāḥ pratyekabuddhabhūtāḥ kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasramabhigaṇayantaḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 12. If, Blessed One, when I have awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, any being could count the number of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) — even if all the beings in a great trichiliocosm, having become <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), were to count for a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 13. sacenme bhagavaṃstasmin buddhakṣetre anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya pramāṇikī me prabhā bhavet, antaśo buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrapramāṇenāpi, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 13. If, Blessed One, when I have awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, my radiance should be limited, even to the extent of a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 227

14. sacenme bhagavannanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya tasmin buddhakṣetre sattvānāṃ pramāṇīkṛtamāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhavet, anyatra praṇidhānavaśena, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 14. If, Blessed One, when I have awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening, the lifespan of the beings in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should be limited in measure, except by the power of their own vow, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text:
15. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasyāyuṣpramāṇaṃ paryantīkṛtaṃ bhavet,
antaśaḥ kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasragaṇayāpi, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 15. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, my own lifespan should be limited, even to the counting of a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 16. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tasmin buddhakṣetre sattvānāmakuśalasya nāmadheyamapi bhavet, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 16. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, even the name of unwholesomeness should exist among the beings in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 17. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya nāpramayeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu aprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhā bhagavanto nāmadheyaṃ parikīrtayeyuḥ, na varṇaṃ bhāṣeran, na praśaṃsāmabhyudīrayeran, na samudīrayeyuḥ,mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 17. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in immeasurable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> should not proclaim my name, should not speak my praise, should not utter and declare my commendation, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 18. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya ye sattvā anyeṣu lokadhātuṣvanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā prasannacittā māmanusmareyuḥ, teṣāṃ cedahaṃ maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtaḥ puraskṛto na puratastiṣṭheyaṃ yadidaṃ cittāvikṣepatāyai, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 18. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, those beings in other world-realms who have generated the mind toward the supreme, perfect awakening and, having heard my name, with serene minds remember me — if I should not stand before them at the time of their death, surrounded and attended by an assembly of monks, for the sake of their mental composure, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 19. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya aprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ye sattvā mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā tatra buddhakṣetre cittaṃ prerayeyuḥ, upapattaye kuśalamūlāni ca pariṇāmayeyuḥ, te tatra buddhakṣetre nopapadyeran, antaśo daśabhiścittotpādaparivartaiḥ sthāpayitvā ānantaryakāriṇaḥ saddharmapratikṣepāvaraṇakṛtāṃśca sattvān, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 19. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, those beings in immeasurable and incalculable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> who, having heard my name, direct their minds toward that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and dedicate their roots of merit for rebirth there — if they should not be reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, even with as few as ten mental resolves, excepting those who have committed the five heinous acts and those who have obstructed the true <s>Dharma</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 20. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājātā bhaveyuḥ,te sarve naikajātipratibaddhāḥ syuranuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau sthāpayitvā praṇidhānaviśeṣān, teṣāmeva bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhānāṃ sarvalokārthasaṃbuddhānāṃ sarvalokābhiyuktānāṃ sarvalokaparinirvāṇābhiyuktānāṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu bodhisattvacaryāṃ caritukāmānāṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ saṃvartukāmānāṃ gaṅgānadīvālukāsamān sattvān anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpakānāṃ bhūyaśca uttaracaryābhimukhānāṃ samantabhadracaryāniryātānām, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 20. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all be bound to the supreme, perfect awakening in one more birth, excepting the specific vows of those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings) who have donned the great armor, who are devoted to the welfare of all worlds, who are engaged in the welfare of all worlds, who are engaged in the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of all worlds, who wish to practice the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct in all world-realms, who wish to attend upon all <s>Buddhas</s>, who establish beings as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in the supreme, perfect awakening, and who are moreover devoted to the higher conduct, who have set forth upon the conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s> — then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening."

children.text: 21. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātā bhaveyuḥ, te sarve ekapurobhaktena anyāni buddhakṣetrāṇi gatvā bahūni buddhaśatāni bahūni buddhasahasrāṇi bahūni buddhaśatasahasrāṇi bahvīrbuddhakoṭīryāvadbahūni buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi nopatiṣṭheran sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ tadidaṃ buddhānubhāvena, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 21. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) cannot, in a single morning meal's time, go to other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> and attend upon many hundreds of <s>Buddhas</s>, many thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, many <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s>, and up to many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, serving them with all provisions of comfort — all through the <s>Buddha's</s> power — then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 22. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasta tatra buddhakṣetre bodhisattvā yathārūpairākārairākāṅkṣeyuḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropayituṃ yadidaṃ suvarṇena vā rajatena vā maṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālasphaṭikamusāragalvalohitamuktāśmagarbhādibhirvā anyatamānyatamaiḥ sarvai ratnairvā sarvagandhapuṣpamālyavilepanadhūpacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāpradīpairvā (
Sukhv, Vaidya 228
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 228]

children.text: ) sarvanṛtyagītavādhairvā, teṣāṃ ca tathārūpā āhārāḥ sahacittotpādānna prādurbhaveyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: all manner of dancing, singing, and music — and if such offerings should not appear spontaneously the moment the thought arises, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

22. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should desire to plant roots of merit in whatever forms they wish — namely with gold, or silver, or gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), conch, crystal, coral, <s>sphaṭika</s> (quartz), <s>musāragalva</s>, red pearl, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald), and other such things, or with any and all jewels, or with all manner of fragrances, flowers, garlands, unguents, incense, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and lamps, or with

children.text: 23. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājātā bhaveyuḥ,te sarva na sarvajñatāsahagatāṃ dharmakathāṃ kathayeyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 23. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, all the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all teach the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) accompanied by omniscience, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 24. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvā evaṃ cittamutpādayeyuḥ - yadihaiva vayaṃ lokadhātau sthitvā aprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhān bhagavataḥ satkuryām gurukuryām mānayema pūjayema yadidaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ puṣpadhūpadīpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākābhirnānāvidhanṛtyagītavādyai ratnavarṣairiti, teṣāṃ ca buddhā bhagavantaḥ sahacittotpādānna pratigṛhṇīyuryadidamanukampāmupādāya, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 24. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should generate the thought: 'If we, while remaining in this very world-realm, were to honor, revere, respect, and worship the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in immeasurable and incalculable <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — namely with robes, alms-food, bedding, medicines for the sick and their requisites, with flowers, incense, lamps, fragrances, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, with various kinds of dancing, singing, and music, and with showers of jewels' — and if those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, should not accept their offerings the moment the thought arises, out of compassion, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 25. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātā bhaveyuḥ, te sarve na nārāyaṇavajrasaṃhatātmabhāvasthāmapratilabdhā bhaveyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 25. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not all attain the bodily strength and constitution that is adamantine like <s>Nārāyaṇa's</s> <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 26. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre yaḥ kaścitsattvo 'laṃkārasya varṇaparyantamudgṛhṇīyāt - antaśo divyenāpi cakṣuṣā evaṃvarṇamevaṃvibhūti idaṃ buddhakṣetramiti nānāvarṇatāṃ jānīyāt, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 26. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, any being in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> could grasp even the extent of the ornaments' splendor — even with the divine eye, knowing 'of such color, of such magnificence is this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>' — could discern the variety of its colors, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 27. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre yaḥ sarvaparīttakuśalamūlo bodhisattvaḥ so 'ntaśo yojanaśatotthitamudāravarṇaṃ bodhivṛkṣaṃ na saṃjānīyāt, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 27. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, any <s>bodhisattva</s> in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, even one of the smallest roots of merit, cannot perceive the great and magnificent <s>Bodhi</s>-tree (tree of awakening) rising at least a hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) high, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 28. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre kasyacitsattvasyoddeśo vā svādhyāyo vā kartavyaḥ syāt, na te sarve pratisaṃvitprāptā bhaveyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 28. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, any being in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> who should study or recite the teachings — if they do not all attain the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 29. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya naivaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhavedyatra samantādaprameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyātulyāparimāṇāni buddhakṣetrāṇi saṃdṛśyeran tadyathāpi nāma parimṛṣṭe ādarśamaṇḍale mukhamaṇḍalam, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 29. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not be so radiant that immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> are seen reflected in it on every side, just as a face is reflected in a polished mirror-disc, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 30. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre dharaṇītalamupādāya yāvadantarīkṣāddevamanuṣyaviṣayātikrāntasyābhijātasya dhūpasya tathāgatabodhisattvapūjāpratyarhasya sarvaratnamayāni nānāsurabhigandhaghaṭikāśatasahasrāṇi sadā nidhūpitānyava na syuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 30. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, from the surface of the earth up to the sky, hundreds of thousands of caskets made of all manner of jewels, filled with the most exquisite fragrances — incense surpassing the range of gods and humans, worthy of worship of <s>Tathāgatas</s> (thus-gone ones) and <s>bodhisattvas</s> — should not always be burning, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 31. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre na sadābhipravṛṣṭānyeva sugandhinānāratnapuṣpavarṣāṇi sadā pravāditāśca manojñasvarā vādyameghā na syuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 31. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, fragrant showers of various jeweled flowers should not always be raining down, and pleasant-sounding music-clouds should not always be playing, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 229

32. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya ye sattvā aprameyāsaṃkhyeyācinyātulyeṣu lokadhātuṣvābhayā sphuṭā bhaveyuḥ, te sarve na devamanuṣyasamatikrāntena sukhena samanvāgatā bhaveyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 32. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the beings who are radiant in the immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, and incomparable world-realms should not all be endowed with bliss surpassing that of gods and humans, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 33. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya samantādaprameyācintyātulyāparimāṇeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā tacchravaṇasahagatena kuśalena jātivyativṛttāḥ santo na dhāraṇīpratilabdhā bhaveyuryāvadbodhimaṇḍaparyantamiti, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 33. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings) in the immeasurable, inconceivable, incomparable, and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> on every side, having heard my name, and having cast off births through the merit associated with that hearing, should not attain <s>dhāraṇī</s> (power of retention) up to the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening), then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 34. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya samantādaprameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyātulyāparimāṇeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu yāḥ striyo mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā pramādaṃ saṃjanayeyuḥ, bodhicittaṃ notpādayeyuḥ, strībhāvaṃ ca na vijugupseran, jātivyativṛttāḥ samānāḥ saceddvitīyaṃ strībhāvaṃ pratilabheran, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 34. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the women in the immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> on every side, having heard my name, should generate delight but not generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), and should not feel revulsion toward the female form — and if, having cast off births, they should again obtain a female body, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 35. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya samantāddaśasu dikṣu aprameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyātulyāparimāṇeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ye bodhisattvā mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā praṇipatya pañcamaṇḍalanamaskāreṇa vandiṣyante te bodhisattvacaryāṃ caranto na sadevakena lokena satkriyeran, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 35. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions on every side, having heard my name, having bowed down with the five-limbed prostration — if those practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct should not be honored by the world including its gods, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 36. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya kasyacidbodhisattvasya cīvaradhāvanaśoṣaṇasīvanarañjanakarma kartavyaṃ bhavet, na tveva navābhijātacīvararatnaiḥ prāvṛtamevātmānaṃ saṃjānīyuḥ sahacittotpādāttathāgatānujñātaiḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 36. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, any <s>bodhisattva</s> should have to wash, dry, sew, or dye robes — and if they do not perceive themselves as wearing newly-arisen jeweled robe-garments, appearing spontaneously the moment the thought arises, by the <s>Tathāgata's</s> authorization, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 37. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre sahotpannāḥ sattvā naivaṃvidhaṃ sukhaṃ pratilabheraṃstadyathāpi nāma niṣparidāhasyārhato bhikṣostṛtīyadhyānasamāpannasya, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 37. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should not attain such bliss as that of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), an <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one) free from all burning, who has entered the third <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation absorption), then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 38. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ,te yathārūpaṃ buddhakṣetre guṇālaṃkāravyūhamākāṅkṣeyuḥ, tathārūpaṃ nānāratnavṛkṣebhyo na saṃjanayeyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 38. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, desiring the array of quality-ornaments of whatever form of <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, should not be able to produce that from the various jeweled trees, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 39. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā anyabuddhakṣetropapannā bodhisattvā indriyabalavaikalyaṃ gaccheyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 39. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> reborn in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, having heard my name, should experience deficiency in their faculties and powers, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 40. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tadanyabuddhakṣetrasthāne bodhisattvā mama nāmadheyasahaśravaṇānna suvibhaktavatīṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabheran, yatra samādhau sthitvā bodhisattvā ekakṣaṇavyatihāreṇa aprameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyātulyāparimāṇān buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyanti, sa caiṣāṃ samādhirantarā vipraṇaśyet, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 40. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, upon hearing my name, should not attain the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Suvibhaktavatī</s> (the Well-Discerned) — a <s>samādhi</s> in which, while abiding therein, a <s>bodhisattva</s> sees immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, and boundless <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in a single moment — and if that <s>samādhi</s> of theirs should be interrupted midway, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 41. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tadanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā tacchravaṇasahagatena kuśalamūlena sattvā nābhijātakulopapattiṃ pratilabheran yāvadbodhiparyantam, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 41. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the beings in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) who hear my name should not, through the root of merit associated with that hearing, attain rebirth in noble families up to the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 230

42. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tadanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ye bodhisattvā mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā tacchravaṇakuśalamūlena yāvadbodhiparyantaṃ te sarve bodhisattvacaryāprītiprāmodyakuśalamūlasamavadhānagatā na bhaveyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 42. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> who hear my name should not all, through the root of merit of that hearing, attain the full endowment of the roots of merit of joy and delight in the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice up to the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 43. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya sahanāmadheyaśravaṇāttadanyeṣu lokadhātuṣu bodhisattvā na samantānugataṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabheran, yatra sthitvā bodhisattvā ekakṣaṇavyatihāreṇa aprameyāsaṃkhyeyācinyātulyāparimāṇān buddhān bhagavataḥ satkurvanti, sa caiṣāṃ samādhirantarā vipraṇaśyedyāvadbodhimaṇḍaparyantam, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 43. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in other world-realms who hear my name should not attain the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Samantānugata</s> (the All-Pervading) — a <s>samādhi</s> in which, while abiding therein, a <s>bodhisattva</s> honors immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, and boundless <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in a single moment — and if that <s>samādhi</s> of theirs should be interrupted midway, up to the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening), then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 44. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājātā bhaveyuḥ te yathārūpāṃ dharmadeśanāmākāṅkṣeyuḥ śrotum, tathārūpāṃ sahacittotpādānna śṛṇuyuḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 44. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, the beings who are reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, desiring to hear whatever kind of <s>Dharma</s> teaching, should not hear it the moment the thought arises, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 45. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya tatra buddhakṣetre tadanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ye ca bodhisattvā mama nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ, te sahanāmadheyaśravaṇānnāvaivartikā bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: 45. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who hear my name should not, upon hearing that name, become <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversible) from the supreme, perfect awakening, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: 46. sacenme bhagavan bodhiprāptasya buddhaśāsturbuddhakṣetreṣu te bodhisattvā mama nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ, te sahanāmadheyaśravanātprathamadvitīyatṛtīyāḥ kṣāntīḥ pratilabheran nāvaivartikā bhaveyurbuddhadharmasaṃghebhyaḥ, mā tāvadahamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhibudhyeyam || Sukhv_8 ||
children.translated_text: 46. If, Blessed One, when I have attained awakening, in the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>-teachers, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who hear my name should not, upon hearing that name, attain the first, second, and third <s>kṣāntis</s> (forbearances) and should not become <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversible) from the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>, then may I not attain the supreme, perfect awakening."

children.text: START Sukhv 9:
children.translated_text: [Section 9:]

children.text: atha khalvānanda sa dharmākaro bhikṣurimānevaṃrūpān praṇidhānaviśeṣānnirdiśya tasyāṃ velāyām buddhānubhāven imā gāthā abhāṣata -
children.translated_text: Then, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Dharmākara</s>, having set forth these specific vow-distinctions of such a form, at that very moment, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, spoke these verses:

children.text: saci mi[siya] viśiṣṭa naivarūpā varapraṇidhāna siyā khu bodhiprāpto /
children.translated_text: "If my distinguished vows are not of such excellent form,

children.text: māha siya gavendrasattvasāro daśabaladhāri atulyadakṣiṇīyaḥ // Sukhv_vs_11 //
children.translated_text: and if upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) I am not the supreme bull among beings, the essence of beings, bearer of the ten powers, of incomparable worthiness of offerings —

children.text: saci mi siya na kṣetra evarūpaṃ bahu adha nānaprabhūtadivyavittam /
children.translated_text: if my <s>kṣetra</s> (field) is not of such a form, with manifold, abundant, divine wealth,

children.text: sukhita naraka yeya duḥkhaprāpto māha siyā ratanāna[loka]rājā // Sukhv_vs_12 //
children.translated_text: bringing happiness to those in the hells who have reached suffering — may I not become the king of the Jewel-realm.

children.text: saci mi upagatasya bodhimaṇḍaṃ daśadiśi pravraji nāmadheyu kṣipram /
children.translated_text: If, upon reaching the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening), my name does not quickly spread through the ten directions,

children.text: pṛthu bahava ananta buddhakṣetrā māha siyā balaprāptu lokanāthaḥ // Sukhv_vs_13 //
children.translated_text: throughout broad, many, infinite <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — may I not become a Lord of the World who has attained the Powers.

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 231
saci khu ahu rameya kāmabhogāṃ smṛtimatiyā gatiyā vihīnu santaḥ /
children.translated_text: If I should delight in sense-pleasures, being devoid of mindfulness and wisdom,

children.text: atula śiva sameyamāna bodhiṃ māha siyā balaprāptu śāstra loke // Sukhv_vs_14 //
children.translated_text: incomparable, auspicious, approaching <s>Bodhi</s> — may I not become a Teacher in the world who has attained the Powers.

children.text: vipulaprabha atulyananta nātha diśi vidiśi sphuri sarvabuddhakṣetrā /
children.translated_text: O Lord of vast, incomparable, and infinite radiance — radiating in every direction and quarter through all <s>buddhakṣetras</s>,

children.text: rāga praśami sarvadoṣamohāṃ narakagatismi praśāmi dhūmaketum // Sukhv_vs_15 //
children.translated_text: may passion be calmed, all vice and delusion; may I extinguish the smoke-bannered fire in the hell-destinies.

children.text: janiya suruciraṃ viśālanetraṃ vidhuniya sarvanarāṇa andhakāram /
children.translated_text: Having produced beautiful, wide eyes, having dispelled the darkness of all beings,

children.text: apaniya su na akṣaṇānaśeṣāṃ upanayi svargagatānanantatejāṃ // Sukhv_vs_16 //
children.translated_text: having removed completely all inopportune rebirths, may I lead them to heavenly destinies of infinite splendor.

children.text: na tapati nabha candrasūryaābhā maṇigaṇa agniprabhā na devatānām /
children.translated_text: Neither the radiance of the moon nor the sun shines in that sky, nor the brilliance of clusters of gems, nor the fire-light of the gods;

children.text: abhibhavati narendra ābha sarvāṃ purimacariṃ pariśuddha ācaritvā // Sukhv_vs_17 //
children.translated_text: the radiance of the Lord of Men surpasses all, having practiced pure conduct in former lives.

children.text: puruṣavaru nidhāna duḥkhitānāṃ diśi vidiśāsu na asti evarūpaḥ /
children.translated_text: O best of men, treasury for the suffering — in all directions and quarters there is no other such as he;

children.text: kuśalaśatasahasrasarvapūrṇa parṣagaro nadi buddhasiṃhanādam // Sukhv_vs_18 //
children.translated_text: fulfilled with hundreds of thousands of all merits, may he roar the lion's roar of the <s>Buddha</s> in the assembly.

children.text: purimajina svayaṃbhu satkaritvā vratatapakoṭi caritva aprameyām /
children.translated_text: Having honored the former <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), the Self-Arisen Ones, having practiced immeasurable <s>koṭis</s> of austerities and vows,

children.text: pravaravarasame 'smi jñānaskandha praṇidhibalapratipūrṇa sattvasāro // Sukhv_vs_19 //
children.translated_text: I am equal to the foremost and supreme in the aggregate of knowledge, my vow-powers fulfilled, the essence of beings.

children.text: yatha bhagava asaṅgajñānadarśī trividha prajānati saṃskṛte narendraḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the Blessed One, the seer of unattached knowledge, knows the threefold conditioned realm, O Lord of Men,

children.text: ahamapi siya tulyadakṣiṇīyo vidupravaro naranāyako narāṇām // Sukhv_vs_20 //
children.translated_text: may I too be of equal worthiness of offerings — the supreme knower, the leader and lord of beings.

children.text: saci mi ayu narendra evarūpā praṇidhi samṛdhyati bodhi prāpuṇitvā /
children.translated_text: If, O Lord of Men, my vows of such form are fulfilled upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening),

children.text: calatu aya sahasralokadhātu kusumapravarṣaṇa bhātu devasaṃghāṃ // Sukhv_vs_21 //
children.translated_text: may this thousandfold world-realm tremble, and may it be adorned with showers of the finest flowers before the host of gods."

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 232
pracalita vasudhā pravarṣi puṣpāḥ tūryaśatā gagane 'tha saṃpraṇeduḥ /
children.translated_text: The earth trembled and flowers rained down, and hundreds of instruments sounded forth in the sky;

children.text: divyaruciracandanasya cūrṇā avakiri caiva bhaviṣya loki buddhaḥ // Sukhv_vs_22 //
children.translated_text: showers of divine, beautiful sandalwood powder fell — and he shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world.

children.text: iti || Sukhv_9 ||
START Sukhv 10:
children.translated_text: [Section 10:]

children.text: evaṃrūpayā ānanda praṇidhānasaṃpadā sa dharmākaro bhikṣurbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ samanvāgato 'bhūt | evaṃrūpayā cānanda praṇidhānasaṃpadā alpakā bodhisattvāḥ samanvāgatāḥ | alpakānāṃ caivaṃrūpāṇāṃ praṇidhīnāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati parīttānām | na punaḥ sarvaśo nāsti | sa khalu punarānanda dharmākaro bhikṣustasya bhagavato lokeśvararājasya tathāgatasya purataḥ sadevakasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ purata imānevaṃrūpān praṇidhānaviśeṣānnirdiśya yathābhūtapratijñāpratipattipratiṣṭhito 'bhūt | sa imāmevaṃrūpāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiṃ buddhakṣetramāhātmyaṃ buddhakṣetrodāratāṃ samudānayan bodhisattvacaryāṃ caran aprameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyātulyāmāpyāparimāṇānabhilāpyāni varṣakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi na jātu kāmavyāpādavihiṃsāvitarkān vitarkitavān,na jātu kāmavyāpādavihiṃsāsaṃjñāmutpāditavān, na jātu rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyasaṃjñāmutpāditavān | sa daharamanohara eva surato 'bhūtsukhasaṃvāso 'dhivāsanajātīyaḥ subhagaḥ supoṣo 'lpecchaḥ saṃtuṣṭaḥ pravivikto 'duṣṭo 'mūḍho 'śaṅko 'jihmo 'śaṭho 'māyāvī sukhilomaḥ priyālāpo nityābhiyuktaḥ śukladharmaparyeṣṭau sunikṣiptadhuraḥ sarvasattvānāmarthāya mahāpraṇidhānaṃ samudānitavān buddhadharmasaṃghācāryopādhyāyakalyāṇamitrasagauravo nityasaṃnaddho bodhisattvacaryāyāmārjavo mārdavo 'kuhako 'nilapako guṇavān pūrvaṃgamaḥ sarvakuśaladharmasamādāpanatāyai śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānabhisaṃskārānutpādavihārairnirmānaḥ svārakṣitavākyaścābhūt | bodhisattvacaryāṃ caran sa yadvākkarmotsṛṣṭamātmaparobhayavyāpādāya saṃvartate, tathāvidhaṃ tyaktvā yadvākkarma svaparobhayahitasukhasaṃvartakaṃ tadevābhiprayuktavān | evaṃ ca samprajāno 'bhūt yadgrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣvavataranna jātu rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmeṣvanunīto 'bhūdapratihataḥ | sa bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ caran svayaṃ ca dānapāramitāyāmacarat parāṃśca tatraiva samādāpitavān, svayaṃ ca śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāpāramitāsvacarat, parāṃśca tatraiva samādāpitavān | tathārūpāṇi ca kuśalamūlāni samudānītavān,yaiḥ samanvāgato yatrayatropapadyate, tatra tatra asyānekāni nidhānakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi dharaṇyāḥ prādurbhavanti | tena bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā tāvadaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāni, yeṣāṃ na sukaraṃ vākkarmaṇā paryantamadhigantum | tāvadaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhā bhagavantaḥ satkṛtā gurukṛtā mānitāḥ pūjitāścīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvasukhopadhānasparśavihāraiḥ pratipāditāḥ | yāvantaḥ sattvāḥ śreṣṭhigṛhapatyamātyakṣatriyabrāhmaṇamahāśālakuleṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, teṣāṃ na sukaro vākkarmanirdeśena paryanto 'dhigantum | evaṃ jāmbūdvīpeśvarāśca pratiṣṭhāpitāścakravartitve lokapālatve śakratve suyāmatve (
Sukhv, Vaidya 233
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 233]

children.text: ) sutuṣitatve sunirmitatve suvaśavartitve devarājatve mahābrahmatve ca pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ | tāvadaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhā bhagavantaḥ satkṛtā gurukṛtā mānitāḥ pūjitāścīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvasukhopadhānasparśavihāraiḥ pratipāditāḥ | yāvantaḥ sattvāḥ śreṣṭhigṛhapatyamātyakṣatriyabrāhmaṇamahāśālakuleṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, teṣāṃ na sukaro vākkarmanirdeśena paryanto 'dhigantum | evaṃ jāmbūdvīpeśvarāśca pratiṣṭhāpitāścakravartitve lokapālatve śakratve suyāmatve sutuṣitatve sunirmitatve vaśavartitve devarājatve mahābrahmatve ca pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ | tāvadaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā buddhā bhagavantaḥ satkṛtā gurukṛtā mānitāḥ pūjitā dharmacakrapravartanārthaṃ cādhīṣṭāḥ,yeṣāṃ na sukaro vākkarmanirdeśena paryanto 'dhigantum | sa evaṃrūpaṃ kuśalaṃ samudānayat,yadasya bodhisattvacaryāṃ carato 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyātulyāmāpyāparimāṇānabhilāpyāni kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi surabhirdivyātikrāntacandanagandho mukhātpravāti sma | sarvaromakūpebhya utpalagandho vāti sma | sarvalokābhirūpaścābhūtprāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ lakṣaṇavyañjanasamalaṃkṛtenātmabhāvena | tasya sarvaratnālakārāḥ sarvavastracīvarābhinirhārāḥ sarvapuṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacchatradhvajapatākābhinirhārāḥ sarvavādyasaṃgītyabhinirhārāśca sarvaromakūpebhyaḥ pāṇitalābhyāṃ ca niścaranti sma | sarvānnapānakhādyabhojyalehyarasābhinirhārāḥ sarvopabhogaparibhogābhinirhārāśca pāṇitalābhyāṃ prasyandantaḥ prādurbhavanti sma | iti hi sarvapariṣkāravaśitāprāptaḥ sa ānanda dharmākaro bhikṣurabhūt pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caran || Sukhv_10 ||
children.translated_text: <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), <s>lokapāla</s> (world-guardian), <s>Śakra</s> (lord of gods), <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Sutuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, <s>Suvaśavartin</s>, king of gods, and <s>Mahābrahmā</s>. He honored, revered, respected, and worshiped immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, attending upon them with robes, alms-food, bedding, medicines for the sick and their requisites, and providing them with all manner of comfortable accommodations. So many beings he established in the families of merchants, householders, ministers, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and great families, that their limit cannot easily be reached by spoken instruction. Likewise, he established beings as lords of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and in the states of <s>cakravartin</s>, <s>lokapāla</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Sutuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, <s>Vaśavartin</s>, king of gods, and <s>Mahābrahmā</s>. He honored, revered, respected, and worshiped immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, and entreated them to turn the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s> — so many that their limit cannot easily be reached by spoken instruction. He accomplished such merit that, as he practiced the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct for immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, boundless, and inexpressible hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), from his mouth wafted a fragrance surpassing divine sandalwood. From all his pores wafted the fragrance of lotus. He was beautiful to behold for all the world — handsome, pleasing to see, endowed with the most auspicious and abundant complexion, adorned in body with the <s>lakṣaṇas</s> (major marks) and <s>vyañjanas</s> (minor marks). From all his pores and from the palms of his hands there issued forth all manner of jeweled ornaments, all manner of garments and robes, all manner of flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, unguents, parasols, banners, and flags, and all manner of musical performances and concerts. From the palms of his hands there issued forth, flowing continuously, all manner of foods, drinks, hard foods, soft foods, savory foods, and delicacies, and all manner of enjoyments and requisites for use. Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Dharmākara</s> had attained mastery over all requisites when previously practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct.

With such a perfection of vows, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Dharmākara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being), was endowed. Few <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, are endowed with such a perfection of vows. Rare is the appearance of such vows in the world — limited in number. Yet it is not that they are entirely absent. Now, <s>Ānanda</s>, the monk <s>Dharmākara</s>, having set forth these specific vow-distinctions of such a form before that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>, before the world with its gods, <s>Māra</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>, before the population including <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, including gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, stood firm in his true vow and practice. Accomplishing such a purification of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), such greatness of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, such excellence of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, and practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct for immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, boundless, and inexpressible hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of years, he never entertained thoughts of sensual desire, malice, or harmfulness; he never generated the perception of sensual desire, malice, or harmfulness; he never generated the perception of forms, sounds, smells, tastes, or tangible objects. While still young, he was charming, agreeable, pleasant in company, of a patient nature, fortunate, easily nourished, of few desires, content, secluded, free from malice, free from delusion, unsuspicious, upright, without deceit, without cunning, gentle in speech, sweet in conversation, ever diligent, devoted to the pursuit of wholesome qualities, bearing his burden well. For the sake of all beings, he generated the great vow — revering the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṅgha</s>, his teachers, preceptors, and spiritual friends, ever armored in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, upright, gentle, without hypocrisy, without pretense, virtuous, a forerunner in urging the undertaking of all wholesome qualities. Dwelling in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>animitta</s> (signlessness), <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness), non-conditioning, and non-arising, he was skilled, and he guarded his speech well. Practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, he abandoned whatever verbal action would conduce to harm for himself, others, or both, and employed only that verbal action which conduces to benefit and happiness for both himself and others. And thus he was fully aware: entering villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals, he was never attracted to the qualities of forms, sounds, smells, tastes, or tangible objects, and remained unimpeded. Practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, he himself practiced the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) and established others in the same; he himself practiced the perfections of morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) and established others in the same. He accomplished such roots of merit that wherever he was reborn, many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of treasures would spring forth from the earth for him. Practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, he established immeasurable and incalculable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of beings in the supreme, perfect awakening — so many that their limit cannot easily be reached by words. He honored, revered, respected, and worshiped immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, attending upon them with robes, alms-food, bedding, medicines for the sick and their requisites, and providing them with all manner of comfortable accommodations. So many beings he established in the families of merchants, householders, ministers, <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors), <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and great families, that their limit cannot easily be reached by spoken instruction. Likewise, he established beings as lords of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (the Rose-Apple Continent) and in the states of

children.text: START Sukhv 11:
children.translated_text: [Section 11:]

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - kiṃ punarbhagavan sa dharmākaro bhikṣurbodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyātītaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ, utāho 'nabhisaṃbuddhaḥ atha pratyutpanno 'bhisaṃbuddha etarhi tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati dharmaṃ ca deśayati? bhagavānāha - na, khalu punarānanda sa tathāgato 'tīto na anāgataḥ | api tveva sa tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddha etarhiṃ tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati dharmaṃ ca deśayati paścimāyāṃ diśi ito koṭīniyutaśatasahasratame ca buddhakṣetre sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvamitābho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'parimāṇairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto 'nantaiḥ śrāvakairanantayā buddhakṣetrasaṃpadā samanvāgataḥ || Sukhv_11 ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: "Is that monk <s>Dharmākara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, one who has awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening in the past and has entered <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation)? Or has he not yet awakened? Or has he awakened in the present and does he now abide, endure, maintain himself, and teach the <s>Dharma</s>?" The Blessed One replied: "No indeed, <s>Ānanda</s> — that <s>Tathāgata</s> is not one of the past, nor one of the future. Rather, that <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one), perfectly and fully awakened one, abides even now in the present, endures, maintains himself, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> — in the western direction, in a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> distant from here, in the world-realm called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss). He is the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitābha</s> (Infinite Light), the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, surrounded and attended by immeasurable <s>bodhisattvas</s>, by infinite <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), and endowed with the infinite perfections of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>."
