children.translated_text: [Section 12:]

children.text: amitā cāsya prabhā yasya na sukaraṃ pramāṇaparyantamadhigantum - iyanti buddhakṣetraśatāni, iyanti buddhakṣetrasahasrāṇi, iyanti buddhakṣetraśatasahasrāṇi, iyanti buddhakṣetrakoṭīni, iyanti buddhakṣetrakoṭīśatāni, iyanti buddhakṣetrakoṭīsahasrāṇi, iyanti buddhakṣetrakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi, iyanti buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi spharitvā tiṣṭhatīti | api tu khalu punarānanda saṃkṣiptena pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamāni buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi tayā tasya bhagavato 'mitābhasya prabhayā sadā sphuṭāni | evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimottarāsvadha ūrdhvaṃ digvidikṣu ca ekaikasyāṃ diśi samantādgaṅgānadīvālukopamāni yāvadbuddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi (
Sukhv, Vaidya 234
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 234]

children.text: ) tasya bhagavato 'mitābhasya prabhayā sadā parisphuṭāni sthāpayitvā buddhān bhagavataḥ pūrvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānena ye vyāmaprabhayā ekadvitricatuḥpañcadaśaviṃśatitriṃśaccatvāriṃśatpañcāśadyojanaprabhayā yojanaśataprabhayā yojanasahasraprabhayā yojanaśatasahasraprabhayā yāvadanekayojanakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraprabhayā vā lokaṃ spharitvā tiṣṭhanti | nāstyānanda upamopanyāso yena śakyaṃ tasyāmitābhasya tathāgatasya prabhāyāḥ pramāṇamudgrahītum | tadanenānanda paryāyeṇa sa tathāgato 'mitābha ityucyate, amitaprabho 'mitaprabhāso 'samāptaprabho 'saṃgataprabhaḥ prabhāśikhotsṛṣṭaprabhaḥ sadivyamaṇiprabho 'pratihataraśmirāgaprabho rājanīyaprabhaḥ premaṇīyaprabhaḥ pramodanīyaprabhaḥ saṃgamanīyaprabha upoṣaṇīyaprabho nibandhanīyaprabho 'tivīryaprabho 'tulyaprabho 'bhibhūyanarendrāmūnnayendraprabhaḥ(?) śrāntasaṃcayendusūryajihmīkaraṇaprabho 'bhibhūya lokapālaśakrabrahmaśuddhāvāsamaheśvarasarvadevajihmīkaraṇaprabha ityucyate | sā ca āryaprabhā vimalā vipulā kāyasukhasaṃjananī cittaudvilyakaraṇī devāsuranāgayakṣagandharvagaruḍamahoragakinnaramanuṣyāmanuṣyāṇāṃ prītiprāmodyasukhakaraṇī kuśalāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ kalyakuśalamimiṇevadviprāmodyakaraṇī(?) ye 'nyeṣvapyanantāparyanteṣu buddhakṣetreṣu | anena cānanda paryāyeṇa tathāgataḥ paripūrṇaṃ kalpaṃ bhāṣyet tasyāmitābhasya tathāgatasya nāma karmopādāya prabhāmārabhya, na ca śaknoti guṇaparyantamadhigantuṃ tasyāḥ prabhāyāḥ, tathāgatasya vaiśāradyopacchedo bhavet | tatkasya hetoḥ? ubhayamapyetadānanda aprameyamasaṃkhyeyamacintyāparyantaṃ yadidaṃ tasya bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasya prabhāguṇavibhūtiḥ, tathāgatasya cānuttaraṃ prajñāpratibhānam || Sukhv_12 ||
children.translated_text: are always pervaded by the radiance of that Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s> — setting aside those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, who by the power of their own former vows abide pervading the world with a radiance extending one <s>vyāma</s> (fathom), or two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty <s>yojanas</s> (leagues), a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, a thousand <s>yojanas</s>, a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, or even many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>yojanas</s>. There is, <s>Ānanda</s>, no simile or comparison by which it would be possible to grasp the measure of the radiance of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>. By this reason, <s>Ānanda</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s> is called <s>Amitābha</s> (Infinite Light) — and also <s>Amitaprabha</s> (Infinite Radiance), <s>Amitaprabhāsa</s> (Infinite Splendor), <s>Asamāptaprabha</s> (Inexhaustible Light), <s>Asaṃgataprabha</s> (Unimpeded Light), <s>Prabhāśikhotsṛṣṭaprabha</s> (Light Emitting Radiant Crests), <s>Sadivyamaṇiprabha</s> (Ever-Divine-Jewel Light), <s>Apratihataraśmirāgaprabha</s> (Unobstructed Ray-Hued Light), <s>Rājanīyaprabha</s> (Delightful Light), <s>Premaṇīyaprabha</s> (Lovable Light), <s>Pramodanīyaprabha</s> (Gladdening Light), <s>Saṃgamanīyaprabha</s> (Inviting Light), <s>Upoṣaṇīyaprabha</s> (Nurturing Light), <s>Nibandhanīyaprabha</s> (Captivating Light), <s>Ativīryaprabha</s> (Supremely Powerful Light), <s>Atulyaprabha</s> (Incomparable Light), <s>Abhibhūyanarendrāmūnnayendraprabha</s> (Light Surpassing All Lords of Men), and <s>Śrāntasaṃcayendusūryajihmīkaraṇaprabha</s> (Light that Eclipses the Moon and Sun with Its Accumulated Splendor), and <s>Abhibhūyalokapālaśakrabrahmaśuddhāvāsamaheśvarasarvadevajihmīkaraṇaprabha</s> (Light that Eclipses All <s>Lokapālas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> Gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and All Deities). That noble radiance is pure, vast, generating bodily bliss and mental elation, producing joy, delight, and happiness for gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, humans, and non-humans, and producing the delight of wholesome joy for beings of virtuous intention in other infinite and boundless <s>buddhakṣetras</s> as well. By this reason too, <s>Ānanda</s>, even if the <s>Tathāgata</s> were to speak for a full <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), taking up the name, deeds, and radiance of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, he could not reach the limit of the qualities of that radiance, and even the <s>Tathāgata's</s> confidence would be exhausted. For what reason? Both of these, <s>Ānanda</s>, are immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, and boundless — namely, the glory of the radiant qualities of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, and the supreme analytical eloquence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

Immeasurable is his radiance, the limit of whose measure is not easily attained — pervading 'so many hundreds of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, so many thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, so many hundreds of thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, so many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, so many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, so many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, so many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, so many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>' — it cannot be expressed thus. But to speak briefly, <s>Ānanda</s>: in the eastern direction, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river are always pervaded by the radiance of that Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s>. Likewise in the southern, western, and northern directions, below, above, and in the intermediate quarters — in each direction on every side, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river

children.text: START Sukhv 13:
children.translated_text: [Section 13:]

children.text: tasya khalu punarānanda amitābhasya tathāgatasyāprameyaḥ śrāvakasaṃgho yasya na sukaraṃ pramāṇamudgrahītum - iyatyaḥ śrāvakakoṭyaḥ,iyanti śrāvakakoṭīśatāni, iyanti śrāvakakoṭīsahasrāṇi, iyanti śrāvakakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi, iyanti kaṃkarāṇi, iyanti bimbarāṇi, iyanti nayutāni, iyantyayutāni, iyantyakṣobhyāṇi, iyanto vivāhāḥ, iyanti srotāṃsi, iyanti ojāṃsi, iyantyaprameyāṇi, iyantyasaṃkhyeyāni, iyantyagaṇyāni, iyantyatulyāni, iyantyacintyānīti | tadyathā ānanda bhikṣurmaudgalyāyana ṛddhivaśitāprāptaḥ | sa ākāṅkṣan trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau yāvanti tārārūpāṇi tāni sarvāṇyekarātridine nagareṇa gaṇayet, evaṃrūpāṇāṃ ca ṛddhimatāṃ koṭīniyutaśatasahasraṃ bhavet, te ca varṣakoṭīniyutaśatasahasramananyakarmaṇā amitābhasya tathāgatasya prathamaśrāvakasaṃnipātaṃ gaṇayeyuḥ | ebhirgaṇayadbhiḥ śatatamo 'pi bhāgo na gaṇito bhavet, sahasratamo 'pi śatasahasratamo 'pi, yāvatkalāmapi upamāmapi upanisāmapi na gaṇito bhavet | tadyathā ānanda mahāsamudrāccaturaśītiyojanasahasrāṇyāvedhena tiryagaprameyāt kaścideva puruṣaḥ śatadhā bhinnayā bālāgrakoṭyā ekamudakabindumabhyutkṣipet, tatkiṃ manyase ānanda katamo 'tra bahutaraḥ - yo vā śatadhā bhinnayā bālāgrakoṭyābhyutkṣipta eka udakabinduḥ, yo vā mahāsamudre 'psakandho 'vaśisṭa iti? ānanda āha - yojanasahasramapi tāvadbhagavan mahāsamudrasya parīttaṃ bhavet kimaṅga punaḥ śatadhā bhinnayā bālāgrakoṭyā (
Sukhv, Vaidya 235
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 235]

children.text: ) utkṣipta eka udakabinduḥ | bhagavānāha - tadyathā sa ekabinduḥ, iyattamaḥ sa prathamasaṃnipāto 'bhūt | tairmaudgalyāyanasadṛśairbhikṣubhirgaṇayadbhistena varṣakoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṇa gaṇitaṃ bhavet, yathā mahāsamudre 'pskandho 'vaśiṣṭaḥ | evamagaṇitaṃ draṣṭavyam | kaḥ punarvādo dvitīyatṛtīyādīnāṃ śrāvakasaṃnipātānām | evamanantāparyantastasya bhagavataḥ śrāvakasaṃgho yo 'prameyāsaṃkhyeya ityeva saṃkhyāṃ gacchati || Sukhv_13 ||
children.translated_text: !" The Blessed One said: "Just as that single drop — such is the extent of that first assembly that would be counted by those monks equal to <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> in that hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of years. And the uncounted remainder should be regarded as the mass of water in the great ocean. What then need be said of the second, third, and subsequent assemblies of <s>śrāvakas</s>? Thus infinite and boundless is the assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s> of that Blessed One — which goes by the designation 'immeasurable and incalculable' indeed."

Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> is immeasurable, and its measure is not easily grasped — 'so many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>, so many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s>, so many thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, so many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, so many <s>kaṃkaras</s>, so many <s>bimbaras</s>, so many <s>nayutas</s>, so many <s>ayutas</s>, so many <s>akṣobhyas</s>, so many <s>vivāhas</s>, so many <s>srotāṃsis</s>, so many <s>ojāṃsis</s>, so many immeasurables, so many incalculables, so many uncountables, so many incomparables, so many inconceivables.' Consider this, <s>Ānanda</s>: the monk <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> has attained mastery over supernatural powers. If he wished, he could count in a single day and night all the star-forms in the great trichiliocosm, counting them city by city. Now suppose there were a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of such supernaturally powerful ones, and they were to count, doing nothing else, for a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of years, counting the first assembly of <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata's</s> <s>śrāvakas</s>. Even with all of them counting, not even a hundredth part would be counted — not a thousandth, not a hundred-thousandth — not even a fraction, a comparison, or an analogy could be reached. Consider this, <s>Ānanda</s>: the great ocean is eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> deep and immeasurable in extent. Now suppose a certain person were to scoop up a single drop of water with a hair-tip split a hundredfold. What do you think, <s>Ānanda</s> — which is greater: the single drop of water scooped up with a hair-tip split a hundredfold, or the mass of water remaining in the great ocean?" <s>Ānanda</s> replied: "Even a thousand <s>yojanas</s> of the great ocean, Blessed One, would be a trifle — how much more so a single drop scooped up by a hair-tip split a hundredfold

children.text: START Sukhv 14:
children.translated_text: [Section 14:]

children.text: aparimitaṃ ca ānanda tasya bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasyāyuḥpramāṇaṃ yasya na sukaraṃ pramāṇamadhigantum, iyanti vā kalpaśatāni, iyanti vā kalpasahasrāṇi, iyanti vā kalpaśatasahasrāaṇi, iyatyo vā kalpakoṭyaḥ, iyanti vā kalpakoṭīśatāni, iyanti vā kalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi, iyanti vā kalpakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi, iyanti vā kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇīti | atha tarhi ānanda aparimitameva tasya bhagavat āyuḥpramāṇamaparyantam | tena sa tathāgato 'mitāyurityucyate | yathā cānanda iha lokadhātau kalpagaṇanāprajñaptisaṃketaḥ, tathā sāṃprataṃ daśa kalpāstasya bhagavato 'mitāyuṣastathāgatasyotpannasya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya || Sukhv_14 ||
children.translated_text: Unlimited, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the measure of the lifespan of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, whose measure is not easily attained — 'so many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, so many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, so many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, so many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, so many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, so many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, so many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, so many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>.' Rather, <s>Ānanda</s>, the measure of the lifespan of that Blessed One is truly unlimited and boundless. For that reason, that <s>Tathāgata</s> is called <s>Amitāyus</s> (Infinite Life). And, <s>Ānanda</s>, according to the conventional reckoning of <s>kalpas</s> in this world-realm, ten <s>kalpas</s> have now elapsed since that Blessed One <s>Amitāyus</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, arose and awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: START Sukhv 15:
children.translated_text: [Section 15:]

children.text: tasya khalu punarānanda bhagavato 'mitābhasya sukhāvatī nāma lokadhāturṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā ca ramaṇīyā ca bahudevamanuṣyākīrṇā ca | tatra khalvānanda lokadhātau na nirayāḥ santi na tiryagyonirna pretaviṣayo nāsurāḥ kāyā nākṣaṇopapattayaḥ | na ca tāni ratnāni loke pracaranti yāni sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau vidyante || Sukhv_15 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the world-realm of that Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s>, called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss), is prosperous, thriving, secure, abundant in provisions, delightful, and filled with many gods and humans. In that world-realm, <s>Ānanda</s>, there are no hells, no animal realm, no domain of hungry ghosts, no bodies of <s>asuras</s> (titans), and no births in inopportune conditions. Nor do those jewels exist in this world that are found in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>.

tasmin khalu punarānanda buddhakṣetre sarvaśaḥ kālaparvatā na santi sarvato ratnaparvatāḥ sarvaśaḥ sumeravaḥ parvatarājāḥ sarvaśaścakravālā mahācakravālāḥ parvatarājāḥ | samantācca tadbuddhakṣetraṃ samaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ pāṇitalajātaṃ nānāvidharatnamaṇicitabhūmibhāgam | evamukte āyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - ye ca punaste bhagavaṃścāturmahārājakāyikā devāḥ sumerupārśvanivāsinastrāyastriṃśā vā sumerumūrdhni nivāsinaḥ, te kutra pratiṣṭhitāḥ? bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase ānanda ye te iha sumeroḥ parvatarājasyopari yāmā devāstuṣitā vā nirmāṇaratayo vā paranirmitavaśavartino vā brahmakāyikā vā brahmapurohitā vā mahābrahmāṇo va yāvadakaniṣṭhā vā, kutra te pratiṣṭhitā iti | ānanda āha - acintyo bhagavan karmaṇāṃ vipākaḥ karmābhisaṃskāraḥ | bhagavānāha - labdhastvayānanda ihācintyaḥ karmaṇāṃ vipākaḥ karmābhisaṃskāro na buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmacintyaṃ buddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtapuṇyānāṃ ca sattvānāmavaropitakuśalamūlānām | tavācintyā puṇyā vibhūtiḥ | ānanda āha - na me 'tra bhagavan kācitkāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā | api tu khalvahamanāgatānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāṅkṣāvimativicikitsānirghātāya tathāgatametadarthaṃ paripṛcchāmi | bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhvānanda,evaṃ te karaṇīyam || Sukhv_17 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there are absolutely no dark mountains; everywhere there are jeweled mountains, everywhere there are <s>Sumerus</s>, the kings of mountains, and everywhere there are <s>Cakravālas</s> and <s>Mahācakravālas</s>, the kings of mountains. And on every side that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is level, delightful, flat as the palm of a hand, its ground studded with various kinds of jewels and gems. When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: "But, Blessed One, where then do the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods who dwell on the slopes of <s>Sumeru</s>, and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods who dwell on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s> — where do they abide?" The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Ānanda</s> — those <s>Yāma</s> gods, <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, and those up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods who dwell above the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, here in this world — where do they abide?" <s>Ānanda</s> replied: "Inconceivable, Blessed One, is the ripening of <s>karma</s> (action), the conditioned formation of <s>karma</s>." The Blessed One said: "You have gained, <s>Ānanda</s>, this insight here — that the ripening of <s>karma</s> and its conditioned formation is inconceivable. But the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-empowerment of the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, and the inconceivable meritorious glory of beings who have planted roots of merit — that you have not yet fully grasped. Your meritorious glory too is inconceivable." <s>Ānanda</s> replied: "I have no doubt, hesitation, or uncertainty about this matter, Blessed One. Rather, I ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about this matter for the purpose of removing the doubts, hesitations, and uncertainties of future beings." The Blessed One said: "Well done, well done, <s>Ānanda</s> — you should indeed do so."

children.text: ) asmākamabhiprāyāḥ paripūryantāmiti, tadā teṣāṃ tādṛśā evābhiprāyā paripūryante | yaścāsāvānanda tasya vāriṇo nirghoṣaḥ sa manojño niścarati, yena sarvāvattadbuddhakṣetramabhijñāpyate | ye ca sattvā nadītīreṣu sthitā ākāṅkṣanti mā asmākamayaṃ śabdaḥ śrotrendriyāvabhāsamāgacchatviti, teṣāṃ na divyasyāpi śrotrendriyasyāvabhāsamāgacchati | yaśca yathārūpaṃ śabdamākāṅkṣati śrotum, sa tathārūpameva manojñaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇoti | tadyathā - buddhaśabdaṃ dharmaśabdaṃ saṃghaśabdaṃ pāramitāśabdaṃ bhūmiśabdaṃ balaśabdaṃ vaiśāradyaśabdamāveṇikabuddhadharmaśabdaṃ pratisaṃvicchabdaṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānabhisaṃskārājātānutpādābhāvanirodhaśabdaṃ śāntapraśāntopaśāntaṃ mahāmaitrīmahākarūṇāmahāmuditāmahopekṣāśabdamanutpattikadharmakṣāntyabhiṣekabhūmipratilambhaśabdam | śrutvā udāraprītiprāmodyaṃ pratilabhate vivekasahagataṃ virāgasahagataṃ śāntasahagataṃ nirodhasahagataṃ dharmasahagataṃ bodhipariniṣpattikuśalamūlasahagataṃ ca | sarvaśaścānanda sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvakuśalaśabdo nāsti, sarvaśo nīvaraṇaśabdo nāsti, sarvaśo 'pāyadurgativinipātaśabdo nāsti, sarvaśo duḥkhaśabdo nāsti | aduḥkhāsukhavedanāśabdo 'pi tāvadānanda tatra nāsti, kutaḥ punarduḥkhaśabdo bhaviṣyati? tadanena ānanda paryāyeṇa sā lokadhātuḥ sukhāvatītyucyate saṃkṣiptena, na punarvistareṇa kalpo 'pyānanda parikṣayaṃ gacchetsukhāvatyā lokadhātoḥ sukhakāraṇeṣu parikīrtyamāneṣu, na tveva śakyaṃ teṣāṃ sukhakāraṇānāṃ paryantamadhigantum || Sukhv_18 ||
children.translated_text: ) 'May our wishes be fulfilled'—then their wishes are fulfilled exactly as desired. And, <s>Ānanda</s>, the sound of those waters issues forth pleasantly, by which that entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) is pervaded. And those beings standing on the riverbanks who wish, 'May this sound not reach our sense of hearing'—for them it does not reach even their divine sense of hearing. And whoever wishes to hear whatever kind of sound, that person hears precisely that kind of pleasant sound. That is to say—the sound of <s>Buddha</s>, the sound of <s>Dharma</s>, the sound of <s>Saṃgha</s>, the sound of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), the sound of the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), the sound of the <s>balas</s> (powers), the sound of the <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the sound of the <s>āveṇika-buddhadharmas</s> (unique qualities of a Buddha), the sound of the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), the sound of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>animitta</s> (signlessness), <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness), <s>anabhisaṃskāra</s> (non-conditioning), <s>ajāta</s> (unborn), <s>anutpāda</s> (non-arising), <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence), and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), the sound of the peaceful, fully pacified, and utterly tranquil, the sound of great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), great <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), and great <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), and the sound of the attainment of <s>anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti</s> (patience of the non-arising of dharmas) and the <s>abhiṣeka-bhūmi</s> (consecration stage). Having heard these, one obtains sublime joy and gladness, accompanied by detachment, accompanied by dispassion, accompanied by peace, accompanied by cessation, accompanied by <s>Dharma</s>, and accompanied by roots of merit leading to the perfection of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). And everywhere in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is no sound of unwholesomeness, nowhere the sound of hindrances, nowhere the sound of the lower realms, evil destinies, or places of ruin, nowhere the sound of suffering. Indeed, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is not even the sound of neutral feeling there—how then could there be the sound of suffering? By this explanation, <s>Ānanda</s>, that world-realm is called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss) in brief; but in detail, even a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), <s>Ānanda</s>, would be exhausted while enumerating the causes of bliss of the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, and still it would not be possible to reach the end of those causes of bliss. [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> 18]

In that world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there flow rivers of various kinds. There are great rivers one <s>yojana</s> wide. There are those up to twenty, thirty, forty, or fifty <s>yojanas</s> wide, and up to twelve <s>yojanas</s> deep. All those rivers flow with pleasant waters, carrying various fragrant waters, carrying clusters of various jewel-strewn flowers, producing various sweet-sounding resonances. From them issues forth a sound as pleasing as that of divine music produced by a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of instruments skillfully played together — such is the sound that issues forth from those great rivers: deep, unknowable, unfathomable, pure, pleasant to the ear, touching the heart, lovable, beautiful, pleasing, delightful, never cloying, not disagreeable to hear — the sound of 'impermanent, peaceful, non-self,' pleasant to hear, which reaches the sense of hearing of those beings. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, on both banks of those great rivers stand rows of various fragrant jeweled trees, from which hang various branches, leaves, flowers, and blossom-clusters. There, those beings who wish to enjoy divine, delightful, and charming sport and recreation on those riverbanks — when they descend into those rivers and wish the water to reach only their ankles, the water stands at ankle-depth. When they wish it to reach their knees, their waist, or their armpits — when they wish it to reach their ears, the water stands at ear-depth, and divine pleasures arise. There, those beings who wish 'let the water be cool' — for them the water becomes cool. Those who wish 'let it be warm' — for them it becomes warm. Those who wish 'let it be both cool and warm' — for them the water becomes both cool and warm, adjusted to their comfort. Those great rivers flow filled with water perfumed with the finest fragrances of divine <s>tamālapatra</s> (bay leaf), <s>agaru</s> (aloe wood), <s>kālānusāri</s> (black aloe), <s>garo</s> (fragrant resin), <s>ragasāra</s> (essence of delight), and <s>candana</s> (sandalwood); they are covered with divine <s>utpalas</s> (blue lotuses), <s>padmas</s> (lotuses), <s>kumudas</s> (night lotuses), <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> (white lotuses), <s>saugandhikas</s> (fragrant water-lilies), and other flowers; they are frequented on their sandy banks by flocks of birds created by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with pleasing songs — <s>haṃsas</s> (wild geese), <s>sārasas</s> (cranes), <s>krauñcas</s> (curlews), <s>cakravākas</s> (ruddy sheldrakes), <s>kāraṇḍavas</s> (ducks), <s>śukas</s> (parrots), <s>śārikās</s> (mynahs), <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoos), <s>kuṇālas</s>, <s>kalaviṅkas</s> (sparrows), <s>mayūras</s> (peacocks), and others; adorned by the attendants of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, with good fords and free of mud, their sandy banks strewn with golden sand. children.text: tasyāṃ khalu punarānanda sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau ye sattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ pratyājaniṣyante, sarve te evaṃrūpeṇa varṇena balena sthāmnā ārohapariṇāhena ādhipatyena puṇyasaṃcayena atiṣṇabhirvastrābharaṇodyānavimānakūṭāgāraparibhogairevaṃrūpaśabdagandharasasparśaparibhogaiḥ evaṃrūpaiśca sarvairapi bhogaparibhogaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ, tadyathāpi nāma devāḥ paranirmitavaśavartinaḥ | na khalu punarānanda sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau sattvā audārikayūṣaphāṇitākārāhāramāharanti | api tu khalu punaryathārūpamevāharamākāṅkṣanti, tathārūpamāhṛtameva saṃjānanti, prīṇitakāyāśca bhavanti prīṇitamānāḥ | na teṣāṃ bhūyaḥ kāye prakṣepaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | te prīṇitakāyāstathārūpāṇi gandhajātānyākāṅkṣanti - īddaśaireva gandhajātairdivyaistadbuddhakṣetraṃ sarvameva nirdhūpitaṃ bhavati | tatra yastaṃ gandhamāghrātukāmo bhavati, tasya sarvaśo gandharvarājño vāsanā na samudācarati | evaṃ ye yathārūpāṇi gandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākātūryāṇyākāṅkṣanti, teṣāṃ tathārūpaiśca taiḥ sarvaṃ tadbuddhakṣetraṃ parisphuṭaṃ bhavati | cīvarāṇyākāṅkṣanti nānāvarṇānyanekaśatasahasravarṇāni, teṣāṃ tādṛśaireva cīvararatnaiḥ sarvaṃ tadbuddhakṣetraṃ parisphuṭaṃ bhavati,prāvṛtameva cātmānaṃ saṃjānanti | te yathārūpāṇyābharaṇānyākāṅkṣanti, tadyathā - śīrṣābharaṇāni vā karṇābharaṇāni vā grīvābharaṇāni vā hastapādābharaṇāni vā yadidaṃ mukuṭāni kuṇḍalāni kaṭakakeyūrāṇi vatsahārā rūcakahārā karṇikā mudrikāḥ svarṇasūtrāṇi mekhalāḥ svarṇasūtāṇi jālāni muktājālāni sarvaratnajālāni svarṇaratnakiṅkiṇījālāni, tathārūpairābharaṇairanekaratnaśatasahasrapratyuptaiḥ sphuṭaṃ (

children.text: ) tadbuddhakṣetraṃ paśyanti yadidamābharaṇavṛkṣāvasaktaiḥ | taiścābharaṇairalaṃkṛtamātmānaṃ saṃjānanti | te yādṛśaṃ vimānamākāṅkṣanti yadvarṇaliṅgasaṃsthānaṃ yāvadārohapariṇāhaṃ nānāratnamayaniryūhaśatasahasrasamalaṃkṛtaṃ nānādivyapuṣpasaṃstīrṇaṃ citropadhānavinyastaparyaṅkam, tādṛśameva vimānaṃ teṣāṃ purataḥ prādurbhavati | teṣu manonirvṛtteṣu vimāneṣu saptasaptāsparasahasraparivṛtāḥ puraskṛtā viharanti krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti || Sukhv_19 ||
children.translated_text: ) that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> adorned with ornaments hanging from the ornament trees. And they perceive themselves as adorned with those ornaments. Whatever kind of palace they desire—of whatever color, form, and shape, of whatever height and breadth, adorned with hundreds of thousands of projections made of various jewels, strewn with various divine flowers, with couches furnished with beautiful cushions—precisely such a palace appears before them. In those palaces, which bring delight to the mind, they dwell surrounded and attended by seven thousand <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), playing, enjoying themselves, and being entertained. [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> 19]

Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, whatever beings have been born or will be born there, all of them are endowed with such form, complexion, strength, vigor, height, and girth, with such sovereignty and accumulation of merit, with such exquisite garments, ornaments, gardens, palaces, and mansions for their enjoyment, with such enjoyments of form, sound, scent, taste, and touch, and with all such pleasures and enjoyments, just like the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the beings in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> do not consume coarse food of soups and molasses. Rather, whatever kind of nourishment they desire, they perceive it as already received, and their bodies become satisfied and content. There is no further need to add anything to their bodies. Being thus satisfied in body, they desire such fragrant substances—and with precisely such divine fragrant substances that entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is entirely suffused with fragrance. For whoever there desires to smell that fragrance, the scent of <s>Gandharvarāja</s> (king of the gandharvas) does not at all arise. Likewise, whatever flowers, garlands, unguents, powders, garments, parasols, banners, flags, or musical instruments they desire, that entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is filled with precisely such things. When they desire garments of various colors, of hundreds of thousands of colors, that entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is filled with precisely such jeweled garments, and they perceive themselves as already clothed. When they desire such ornaments—namely head ornaments, ear ornaments, neck ornaments, hand and foot ornaments, such as diadems, earrings, bracelets, armlets, necklaces, pendants, rings, gold chains, girdles, gold threads, nets, pearl nets, nets of all jewels, nets of golden jewel-bells—with such ornaments set with hundreds of thousands of various jewels, they behold (

children.text: START Sukhv 20:
children.translated_text: [Section 20:]

children.text: na ca tatra lokadhātau devānāṃ vā manuṣyāṇāṃ vā nānātvamasti anyatra saṃvṛtivyavahāreṇa devamanuṣyāviti saṃkhyāṃ gacchanti | tadyathā ānanda rājñaścakravartinaḥ purato manuṣyahīno manuṣyapretako na bhāsate na tapate na virocate, na ca bhavati viśārado na prabhāśvaraḥ, evameva devānāṃ paranirmitavaśavartināṃ purataḥ śakro devānāmindro na bhāsate na tapate na virocate yadidamudyānavimānavastrābharaṇairādhipatyena ṛddhyā vā prātihāryeṇa vā aiśvaryeṇa vā ānanda, sa khalu dharmābhisamayena dharmaparibhogeṇa vā | tatra ānanda yathā devāḥ parinirmitavaśavartinaḥ, evaṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau manuṣyā draṣṭavyāḥ || Sukhv_20 ||
children.translated_text: And in that world-realm there is no difference between gods and humans; they are counted as 'gods and humans' only by way of conventional designation. Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, before a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), a person of inferior appearance, a wretched human, neither shines, nor blazes, nor glows—even so, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, does not shine, nor blaze, nor glow before the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, whether in gardens, palaces, garments, ornaments, sovereignty, supernatural power, miraculous display, or mastery, <s>Ānanda</s>—except through realization of <s>Dharma</s> or enjoyment of <s>Dharma</s>. Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, just as the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods are, so should the humans in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> be regarded. [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> 20]

children.text: START Sukhv 21:
children.translated_text: [Section 21:]

children.text: tasyāṃ khalu punarānanda sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau pūrvāhṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite samantāccaturdiśamākulāḥ samākulā vāyavo vānti | teṣāṃ ratnavṛkṣāṇāṃ citrān darśanīyān nānāvarṇānanekavṛntān nānāsurabhidivyagandhaparivāsitān kṣobhayanti saṃkṣobhayanti īrayanti samīrayanti yato bahūni puṣpaśatāni tasyāṃ ratnamayyāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ prapatanti manojñagandhāni darśanīyāni | taiśca puṣpaistadbuddhakṣetraṃ samantātsaptapauruṣaṃ saṃskṛtarūpaṃ bhavati | tadyathāpi nāma puruṣaḥ kuśalaḥ pṛthivyāṃ puṣpasaṃstaraṃ saṃstṛṇuyāt, ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ samaṃ racayetsucitraṃ darśanīyam, evameva tadbuddhakṣetraṃ taiḥ puṣpairnānāgandhavarṇaiḥ samantātsaptapauruṣaṃ sphuṭaṃ bhavati | tāni ca puṣpajātāni mṛdūni kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśāni aupamyamātreṇa, yāni nikṣipte pāde caturaṅgulamavanamanti, utkṣipte pāde caturaṅgulamevonnamanti | nirgate punaḥ pūrvāhṇakālasamaye tāni puṣpāṇi niravaśeṣamantardhīyante | athe tadbuddhakṣetraṃ viviktaṃ ramyaṃ śubhaṃ bhavatyaparikliṣṭaiḥ pūrvapuṣpaiḥ | tataḥ punarapi samantāccaturdiśaṃ vāyavo vānti, ye pūrvavadabhinavāni puṣpāṇyabhiprakiranti | yathā pūrvāhṇe, evaṃ madhyāhnakālasamaye saṃdhyāyāṃ rātryāḥ prathame yāme madhyame yāme paścime yāme | taiśca vātairvāyadbhirnānāgandhaparivāsitaiste sattvāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ santaḥ evaṃ sukhasamarpitā bhavanti tadyathāpi nāma nirodhasamāpanno bhikṣuḥ || Sukhv_21 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, when the time of early morning arrives, winds blow from the four directions, filled and laden. They stir and shake those jeweled trees, causing their marvelous, beautiful flowers of various colors, many-stalked, and permeated with various divine fragrances to tremble, and hundreds of flowers fall upon that jeweled great earth, pleasant in fragrance and beautiful to behold. With those flowers, that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is everywhere covered to the height of seven men, appearing as if artfully arranged. Just as a skilled person might spread a carpet of flowers on the ground and arrange it evenly with both hands, marvelously beautiful to behold—even so, that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is everywhere covered to the height of seven men with those flowers of various fragrances and colors. And those flowers are soft, with the pleasant touch of <s>Kācilindika</s> cloth, by way of comparison; when a foot is placed down they sink four finger-breadths, and when a foot is lifted they spring back up four finger-breadths. When the early morning time has passed, those flowers disappear completely without remainder. Then that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> becomes pure, delightful, and beautiful, unencumbered by the former flowers. Then again the winds blow from the four directions, scattering fresh flowers as before. As in the early morning, so also at midday, at twilight, in the first watch of the night, the middle watch, and the last watch. And those beings, touched by those winds blowing with their various fragrances, are immersed in such bliss as is experienced by a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who has entered the <s>nirodha-samāpatti</s> (attainment of cessation). [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> 21]

children.text: START Sukhv 22:
children.translated_text: [Section 22:]

children.text: tasmiścānanda buddhakṣetre sarvaśo 'gnisūryacandragrahanakṣatratārārūpāṇāṃ tamondhakārasya nāmadheyaprajñapraptirapi nāsti | sarvaśo rātriṃdivaṃ prajñaptirapi nāsti anyatra tathāgatavyavahārāt, sarvaśaścārāmaparigrahasaṃjñā nāsti || Sukhv_22 ||
children.translated_text: And in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is absolutely no designation or concept of the forms of fire, sun, moon, planets, constellations, or stars, nor of darkness or gloom. There is absolutely no designation of night and day, except by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s conventional usage, and there is absolutely no notion of attachment to gardens or possessions. [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> 22]

children.text: START Sukhv 24:
children.translated_text: [Section 24:]

children.text: tasmin khalu punarānanda buddhakṣetre ye sattvā upapannā utpadyante utpasyante, sarve te niyatāḥ samyaktve yāvannirvāṇam | tatkasya hetoḥ? nāsti tatra dvayo rāśyorvyavasthānaṃ prajñaptirvā yadidamaniyatasya vā mithyātvaniyatasya vā | tadanenāpyānanda paryāyeṇa sā lokadhātuḥ sukhāvatītyucyate saṃkṣiptena, na punarvistareṇa | kalpo 'pyānanda parikṣīyeta sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau sukhakāraṇeṣu parikīrtyamāneṣu, na ca teṣāṃ sukhakāraṇānāṃ śakyaṃ paryantamadhigantum || Sukhv_24 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), whatever beings have been born, are being born, or will be born — they are all assured of the right course up to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> (final liberation). For what reason? There is no establishment or designation there of two groups — namely, those who are undetermined or those fixed in wrong views. By this reason too, <s>Ānanda</s>, that world-realm is called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss) in brief, though not in full. Even a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), <s>Ānanda</s>, would be exhausted while enumerating the causes of happiness in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, yet the limit of those causes of happiness cannot be reached. || Sukhv_24 ||

children.text: START Sukhv 25:
children.translated_text: [Section 25:]

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
children.translated_text: Then at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses —
