children.translated_text: Even if all beings were to become happy, endowed with pure knowledge and skilled in the highest truth,

children.text: te kalpakoṭīmatha vāpi cottariṃ sukhāvatīvarṇa prakāśayeyuḥ // Sukhv_vs_23 //
children.translated_text: and for <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) or even more, were to proclaim the glories of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>,

children.text: kṣaye kalpakoṭī vajre surāśca sukhāvatīye na ca varṇasāruḥ /
children.translated_text: even when <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> are exhausted, firm as a diamond, and the gods too — the glory of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> would not be exhausted,

children.text: kṣayaṃ na gacchetpratibhā ca teṣāṃ prakāśayantāna tu varṇa nānāṃ // Sukhv_vs_24 //
children.translated_text: nor would the eloquence of those proclaiming its various glories come to an end.

children.text: ye lokadhātū paramāṇusādṛśāṃśchidyeya bhidyeya rajaśca kuryāt /
children.translated_text: If one were to split and break apart world-realms as numerous as atoms and reduce them to dust,

children.text: ato bahū uttari lokadhātu pūreta dānaṃ ratanāhi dadyāt // Sukhv_vs_25 //
children.translated_text: and fill even more world-realms than these with gifts of jewels,

children.text: naitā kalāpi upamāpi tasya puṇyasya bhontī pṛthulokadhātavaḥ /
children.translated_text: not even a fraction or a comparison of that merit would these vast world-realms equal —

children.text: ye lokadhātūya sukhāvatīye śrutvaiva nāmaṃ bhavatīha puṇyam // Sukhv_vs_26 //
children.translated_text: the merit that arises simply from hearing the name of the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>.

children.text: tato bahū puṇya bhaveta teṣāṃ ye śraddhate jinavacanaṃ saprajñāḥ /
children.translated_text: Far greater merit would accrue to those who, endowed with wisdom, have faith in the word of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror),

children.text: śraddhā hi mūlaṃ jagatasya prāptaye tasmāddhi śrutvā vicitiṃ vinodayet // Sukhv_vs_27 //
children.translated_text: for faith is the root for attaining the goal of the world; therefore, having heard, one should dispel doubt.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus. ||

children.text: evamaprameyaguṇavarṇā ānanda sukhāvatī lokadhātuḥ || Sukhv_25 ||
children.translated_text: Of such immeasurable qualities and glory, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. || Sukhv_25 ||

children.text: START Sukhv 26:
children.translated_text: [Section 26:]

children.text: tasya khalu punarānanda bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasya daśasu dikṣu ekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukāsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā buddhā bhagavanto nāmadheyaṃ (
Sukhv, Vaidya 241
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 241]

children.text: ) parikīrtayante, varṇaṃ bhāṣante, yaśaḥ prakāśayanti, guṇamudīrayanti | tatkasya hetoḥ? ye kecitsattvāstasya bhagavato 'mitābhasya nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇvanti, śrutvā cāntaśa ekacittotpādamapyadhyāśayena prasādasahagatena cittamutpādayanti,te sarve 'vaivartikatāyāṃ santyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ || Sukhv_26 ||
children.translated_text: they extol his glory, proclaim his fame, and declare his virtues. For what reason? Whatever beings hear the name of that Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s>, and having heard it, generate even a single thought with a mind accompanied by faith and deep aspiration — they are all assured of non-retrogression from the supreme, perfect awakening. || Sukhv_26 ||

Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in the ten directions, in each and every direction, in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river proclaim the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>

children.text: START Sukhv 27:
children.translated_text: [Section 27:]

children.text: ye cānanda kecitsattvāstaṃ tathāgataṃ punaḥ satkāramanasikariṣyanti, bahvaparimitaṃ kuśalamūlamavaropayiṣyanti bodhaye cittaṃ pariṇāmya, tatra ca lokadhātāvupapattaye praṇidhāsyanti, teṣāṃ so 'mitābhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite 'nekabhikṣugaṇaparivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ sthāsyati | tataste taṃ bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasannacittāścyutāḥ santastatraiva sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | yaśca ānanda ākāṅkṣeta kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā kimityahaṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme tamamitābhaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyeyamiti, tenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya adhyāśayātiśayatayā saṃtatyā tasmin buddhakṣetre cittaṃ saṃpreṣya upapattaye kuśalamūlāni ca pariṇāmayitavyāni || Sukhv_27 ||
children.translated_text: And, <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever beings will honor and attend to that <s>Tathāgata</s>, will plant abundant and immeasurable roots of merit, dedicating their minds toward awakening, and will aspire to be reborn in that world-realm — for them, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one), the perfectly and fully awakened one, will stand before them at the time of death, surrounded and attended by a multitude of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). And they, having seen that Blessed One, with serene minds, upon passing away, will be reborn in that very world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. And, <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever son or daughter of a good family should aspire thus: 'May I, in this very life, see that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>' — such a one should generate the mind of supreme, perfect awakening, and with the excellence of deep aspiration, should continuously direct the mind toward that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and dedicate roots of merit for rebirth there. || Sukhv_27 ||

children.text: START Sukhv 28:
children.translated_text: [Section 28:]

children.text: ye punastaṃ tathāgataṃ na bhūyo manasikariṣyanti, na ca bahvaparimitaṃ kuśalamūlamabhīkṣṇamavaropayiṣyanti, teṣāṃ tādṛśenaiva so 'mitābhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho varṇasaṃsthānārohapariṇāhena bhikṣusaṃghaparivāreṇa ca tādṛśa eva buddhinirmito maraṇakālasamaye purataḥ sthāsyati | te tenaiva tathāgatadarśanaprasādālambanena samādhinā apramuṣitayā smṛtyā cyutāstatraiva buddhakṣetre pratyājaniṣyanti || Sukhv_28 ||
children.translated_text: But those who will not greatly attend to that <s>Tathāgata</s>, and will not frequently plant abundant and immeasurable roots of merit — for them, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, with the same form, appearance, stature, and proportions, and with the same retinue of the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (monastic community), will stand before them at the time of death as a mind-created emanation. They, by the very same <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) supported by the faith arising from seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with unconfused mindfulness, upon passing away, will be reborn in that very <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. || Sukhv_28 ||

children.text: START Sukhv 29:
children.translated_text: [Section 29:]

children.text: ye punarānanda sattvāstaṃ tathāgataṃ daśacittotpādātsamanusmariṣyanti, spṛhāṃ ca tasmin buddhakṣetra utpādayiṣyanti, gambhīreṣu ca dharmeṣu bhāṣyamāṇeṣu tuṣṭiṃ pratilapsyante, na vipatsyante,na viṣādamāpatsyante,na saṃsadanamāpatsyante, antaśa ekacittotpādenāpi taṃ tathāgataṃ manasikariṣyanti, spṛhāṃ cotpādayiṣyanti tasmin buddhakṣetre, te 'pi svapnāntaragatā amitābhaṃ tathāgataṃ drakṣyanti, sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante, avaivartikāśca bhaviṣyantyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ || Sukhv_29 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever beings will recollect that <s>Tathāgata</s> with the arising of ten thoughts, and will generate aspiration for that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, and when profound <s>dharmas</s> (teachings) are being spoken will gain satisfaction and will not waver, will not fall into despair, will not lose heart — even with a single arising of thought they will attend to that <s>Tathāgata</s> and will generate aspiration for that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> — they too, in their dreams, will see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, will be reborn in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, and will become irreversible from the supreme, perfect awakening. || Sukhv_29 ||

children.text: START Sukhv 30:
children.translated_text: [Section 30:]

children.text: imaṃ khalvānanda arthavaśaṃ saṃpaśya tathāgatā daśasu dikṣu aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāsu lokadhātuṣu tasyāmitābhasya tathāgatasya nāmagheyaṃ parikīrtayanto varṇaṃ ghoṣayantaḥ saṃpraśaṃsāmabhyudīrayanti | tasmin khalu punarānanda buddhakṣetre daśabhyo digbhya ekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā bodhisattvāstamamitābhaṃ tathāgatamupasaṃkramanti darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya paripraśnīkaraṇāya, taṃ ca bodhisattvagaṇaṃ tāṃśca buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadviśeṣān draṣṭum || Sukhv_30 ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this purpose, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions, in immeasurable and incalculable world-realms, proclaim the name of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, extol his glory, and utter his praise. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, from the ten directions, in each direction, <s>bodhisattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river approach that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s> — for the purpose of seeing, honoring, attending upon, and questioning him, and to behold that assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and the special excellences of the ornamental arrays and qualities of those <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. || Sukhv_30 ||

children.text: START Sukhv 31:
children.translated_text: [Section 31:]

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā paridīpayannimā gāthā abhāṣata -
children.translated_text: Then at that time, the Blessed One, illuminating this very meaning with even greater measure, spoke these verses —

children.text: yathaiva gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā buddhāna kṣetrā amitāyunāyakam // Sukhv_vs_28 //
children.translated_text: Just as from <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, [they come] to the Lord <s>Amitāyus</s>,

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 242
bahupuṣpapūṭī gṛhītva te nānāvarṇaṃ surabhī manoramāṃ /
children.translated_text: taking up abundant handfuls of flowers of various colors, fragrant and delightful,

children.text: okiranti naranāyakottamaṃ amitāyuṃ naradevapūjitam // Sukhv_vs_29 //
children.translated_text: they scatter them upon the supreme Lord of Men, <s>Amitāyus</s>, honored by gods and humans.

children.text: tatha dakṣiṇapaścimottarāsu buddhāna kṣetrā daśatāsu yāttakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise from the southern, western, and northern directions, from <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in all ten quarters, as many as there are,

children.text: yato yato āgami buddha vandituṃ sabodhisattvā amitāyunāyakam // Sukhv_vs_30 //
children.translated_text: from wherever they come, <s>Buddhas</s> together with <s>bodhisattvas</s> come to honor the Lord <s>Amitāyus</s>.

children.text: bahugandhāpūṭī gṛhitvā nānāvarṇa surabhī manoramāṃ /
children.translated_text: Taking up abundant handfuls of fragrances of various colors, fragrant and delightful,

children.text: okiranti naranāyakottamaṃ amitāyuṃ naradevapūjitam // Sukhv_vs_31 //
children.translated_text: they scatter them upon the supreme Lord of Men, <s>Amitāyus</s>, honored by gods and humans.

children.text: pūjitva vā te bahubodhisattvā vanditva pādāmamitaprabhasya /
children.translated_text: Having worshiped, those many <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having bowed at the feet of <s>Amitaprabha</s> (Infinite Light),

children.text: pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vadanti caivaṃ aho 'dbhutaṃ śobhati buddhakṣetram // Sukhv_vs_32 //
children.translated_text: and having circumambulated, they speak thus: "How wondrous — this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shines!"

children.text: te puṣpapūṭīhi punokiranti udagracittā atulāya prītiye /
children.translated_text: They scatter handfuls of flowers again with exalted minds, for incomparable joy,

children.text: kāmaṃ prabhāṣanti purasta nāyake asmāpi kṣetraṃ siya evarūpam // Sukhv_vs_33 //
children.translated_text: and freely proclaim before the Lord: "May our field too become of such a form!"

children.text: ye puṣpapūṭā iti kṣipta tatra chatraṃtayā saṃsthihi yojanāśatam /
children.translated_text: The handfuls of flowers thus scattered there stand in a parasol-like formation, a hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in extent,

children.text: svalaṃkṛtaṃ śobhati citraravato chādante buddhasya samanta kāyam // Sukhv_vs_34 //
children.translated_text: beautifully adorned, radiant with wondrous colors, covering the body of the <s>Buddha</s> on all sides.

children.text: te bodhisattvā tathā satkaritvā kathaṃ karontī iti tuṣṭa tatra /
children.translated_text: Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having thus honored him, delighted there at what has been accomplished —

children.text: sulabdha lābhāḥ khalu tehi sattvaiḥ yehī śrutaṃ nāma narottamasya // Sukhv_vs_35 //
children.translated_text: "Well-gained indeed is the gain by those beings who have heard the name of the Supreme among Men!"

children.text: asmehi pī lābha sulabdhapūrvā yadā gatāsya ima buddhakṣetram /
children.translated_text: "By us too a gain has been well-gained, since we have come to this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>,

children.text: paśyātha svapnopama maitra kīdṛśaṃ yatkalpitaṃ kalpasahasra śāstuḥ // Sukhv_vs_36 //
children.translated_text: behold, O friends, like a dream — how wondrous is what the Teacher has fashioned over thousands of <s>kalpas</s>!"

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 243
paśyātha buddhā vara puṇyarāśiḥ parivṛto śobhati bodhisattvaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Behold the <s>Buddha</s>, the supreme heap of merit — he shines, surrounded by <s>bodhisattvas</s>,

children.text: amitābhasya ābhā amitā ca tejā amitaṃ ca āyūramitaśca saṃghaḥ // Sukhv_vs_37 //
children.translated_text: the radiance of <s>Amitābha</s> is infinite, his splendor infinite, his life infinite, and his assembly infinite."

children.text: smitaṃ karotī amitāyunāthaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśakoṭīnayutāna arciṣām /
children.translated_text: The Lord <s>Amitāyus</s> makes a smile, and thirty-six <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of rays,

children.text: ye niścaritvā mukhamaṇḍalātaḥ sphūranti kṣetrāṇi sahasrakoṭīḥ // Sukhv_vs_38 //
children.translated_text: issuing forth from the orb of his face, spread through a thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>.

children.text: tāḥ sarvasūrīḥ punaretya tatra mūrdhe ca astaṃ gami nāyakasya /
children.translated_text: All those rays, returning there, set upon the crown of the Lord's head,

children.text: devā manuṣyā janayanti prītiṃ arcistadā asyamidāṃ viditvā // Sukhv_vs_39 //
children.translated_text: and gods and humans generate joy, knowing this to be the radiance of that occasion.

children.text: uttiṣṭhate buddhasuto mahāyaśā nātha so hi avalokiteśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: There arises the greatly renowned son of the <s>Buddha</s> — he is the Lord <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>,

children.text: ko heturatra bhagavaṃ kaḥ pratyayo yena smitaṃ kurvasi lokanātha // Sukhv_vs_40 //
children.translated_text: What is the reason here, Blessed One, what is the cause by which you smile, O Lord of the World?

children.text: taṃ vyākarohī yatra so 'rthakovido hitānukampī bahusattvamocakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Prophesy that, O Knower of Meaning, compassionate for the welfare of beings, liberator of many beings,

children.text: śrutveti vācaṃ paramāṃ manoramāṃ udagracittā bhaviṣyanti sattvāḥ // Sukhv_vs_41 //
children.translated_text: having heard that supreme and delightful speech, beings will become elated in mind.

children.text: ye bodhisattvā bahulokadhātutaḥ sukhāvatīṃ prasthita buddha paśyatāṃ /
children.translated_text: Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have set forth from many world-realms toward <s>Sukhāvatī</s> — let them behold the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: te śrutvā prītiṃ vipulāṃ janetvā kṣipramimaṃ kṣetra vilokayeyuḥ // Sukhv_vs_42 //
children.translated_text: having heard, they shall generate abundant joy and quickly behold this field.

children.text: āgatya ca kṣetramidaṃ udāraṃ ṛddhībalaṃ prāpuṇi kṣiprameva /
children.translated_text: Having come to this sublime field, they swiftly attain the power of supernatural abilities,

children.text: divyaṃ ca cakṣustatha śrotra divyaṃ jātismarāḥ pāramikovidāśca // Sukhv_vs_43 //
children.translated_text: and the divine eye and likewise the divine ear, recollection of past births, and skill in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).

children.text: amitāyu buddhastada vyākaroti mama hyayaṃ praṇidhi babhūva pūrvam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> (Infinite Life) then prophesies: "This indeed was my former <s>praṇidhi</s> (vow),

children.text: kathaṃ pi sattvā śruṇiyāni nāma vrajeyu kṣetraṃ mama nityameva // Sukhv_vs_44 //
children.translated_text: that somehow beings may hear my name and may come to my field eternally."

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 244
sa me ayaṃ praṇidhi prapūrṇa śobhanā sattvāśca ebhi bahulokadhātutaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This splendid <s>praṇidhi</s> (vow) of mine is now fulfilled, and beings come from many world-realms,

children.text: āgatya kṣipraṃ mama antikasmiṃ avaivartikā bhontiha ekajātiyā // Sukhv_vs_45 //
children.translated_text: having come quickly to my presence, they become <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversible) here, with but one birth remaining."

children.text: tasmādya icchatiha bodhisattvaḥ mamāpi kṣetraṃ siya evarūpam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, whatever <s>bodhisattva</s> here wishes — 'May my field too be of such a form,'

children.text: ahaṃ pi sattvān bahu mocayeyaṃ nāmena ghoṣeṇa tha darśanena // Sukhv_vs_46 //
children.translated_text: 'May I too liberate many beings by name, by proclamation, and by sight' —

children.text: sa śīghraśīghraṃ tvaramāṇarūpaḥ sukhāvatīṃ gacchatu lokadhātum /
children.translated_text: let him go quickly, quickly, in haste, to the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>,

children.text: gattvā ca pūrvamamitaprabhasya pūjetu buddhāna sahasrakoṭīḥ // Sukhv_vs_47 //
children.translated_text: and having first gone before <s>Amitaprabha</s> (Infinite Radiance), let him worship thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>."

children.text: buddhāna koṭī bahu pūjayitvā ṛddhībalena bahu kṣetra gattvā /
children.translated_text: Having worshiped many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, having gone to many fields by the power of supernatural abilities,

children.text: kṛtvāna pūjāṃ sugatāna santike bhaktyā gamiṣyanti sukhāvatītaḥ // Sukhv_vs_48 //
children.translated_text: having made offerings in the presence of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones), they shall go forth from <s>Sukhāvatī</s> with devotion.

children.text: iti || Sukhv_31 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends [Section 31].

children.text: START Sukhv 32:
children.translated_text: [Section 32:]

children.text: tasya khalu punarānanda amitāyuṣastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya bodhivṛkṣaḥ | sa daśa yojanaśatānyuccaistvena,aṣṭau yojanaśatānyabhipralambitaśākhāpatrapalāśaḥ pañcayojanaśatamūlārohapariṇāhaḥ sadāpatraḥ sadāpuṣpaḥ sadāphalo nānāvarṇo 'nekaśatasahasravarṇo nānāpatro nānāpuṣpo nānāphalo nānāvicitrabhūṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtaścandrabhāsamaṇiratnaparisphuṭaḥ śakrābhilagnamaṇiratnavicitritaścintāmaṇiratnākīrṇaḥ sāgaravaramaṇiratnasuvicitrito divyasamatikrāntaḥ svarṇasūtrābhipralambito rucakahāraratnahāravatsahārakaṭakahāralohitamuktāhāranīlamuktāhārasiṃhalatāmekhalākalāparatnasūtrasarva-ratnavastuśatābhivicitritaḥ svarṇajālamuktājālasarvaratnajālakiṅkiṇījālatato makarasvastikanandyāvartacandrasamalaṃkṛtaḥ kiṅkiṇīmaṇijālasauvarṇasarvaratnālaṃkāravibhūṣito yathāśayasattvavijñaptisamalaṃkṛtaśca | tasya khalu punarānanda bodhivṛkṣasya vātasamīritasya yaḥ śabdo ghoṣo niścarati so 'parimāṇāṃllokadhātūn vijñāpayati | tatrānanda yeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sa bodhivṛkṣaḥ śrotrāvabhāsamāgacchati, teṣāṃ śrotrarogo na pratikāṅkṣitavyo yāvadbodhiparyantam | yeṣāmaprameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyātulyāmāpyāparimāṇānabhilāpyānāṃ sattvānāṃ sa bodhivṛkṣaścakṣuṣa ābhāsamāgacchati, teṣāṃ cakṣūrogo na pratikāṅkṣitavyo yāvadbodhiparyantam | ye khalu punarānanda sattvāstato bodhivṛkṣādgandhaṃ jighranti, teṣāṃ yāvadbodhiparyantaṃ na jātu ghrāṇaroagaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ | ye sattvāstato bodhivṛkṣatphalānyāsvādayanti, teṣāṃ yāvadbodhiparyantaṃ na jātu jihvārogaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ | ye sattvāstasya bodhivṛkṣasyābhayā sphuṭā (
Sukhv, Vaidya 245
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 245]

children.text: ) bhavanti, teṣāṃ yāvadbodhiparyantaṃ na jātu kāyarogaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ | ye ca khalu punarānanda sattvāstaṃ bodhivṛkṣaṃ dharmato nidhyāyanti, teṣāṃ tata upādāya yāvadbodhiparyantaṃ na jātu cittavikṣepaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ | sarve ca te sattvāḥ sahadarśanāttasya bodhivṛkṣasyāvaivartikāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante yadutānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ | tisraśca kṣāntīḥ pratilabhante yadidaṃ ghoṣānugāmanulomikīmanutpattikadharmakṣāntiṃ ca tasyaivāmitāyuṣastathāgatasya pūrvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānena pūrvajinakṛtādhikāratayā pūrvapraṇidhānaparicaryayā ca susamāpyayā subhāvitayānūnāvikalatayā || Sukhv_32 ||
children.translated_text: ) that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s>, no bodily disease is to be anticipated up until the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, for those beings who contemplate that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, from that point onward no mental distraction is to be anticipated up until the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>. And all those beings, from the very moment of seeing that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s>, stand firm in <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversibility) regarding the supreme, perfect awakening. And they attain three kinds of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience): namely, <s>ghoṣānugā</s> (sound-following patience), <s>anulomikī</s> (conforming patience), and <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas) — through the empowerment of the former vows of that very <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, through the superior foundation laid by former <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), and through the well-accomplished, well-cultivated, complete and undeficient fulfillment of former vow-practice.

Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s> (Bodhi tree) of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one — it is a thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in height, eight hundred <s>yojanas</s> in the spread of its hanging branches and foliage, five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in the circumference of its root-base. It is ever in leaf, ever in flower, ever in fruit, of various colors and hundreds of thousands of hues, of various leaves, various flowers, various fruits, adorned with manifold and beautiful ornaments, studded with <s>candrabhāsamaṇi</s> (moonlight) jewels, decorated with <s>śakrābhilagnamaṇi</s> (Indra's-best) jewels, covered with <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) jewels, beautifully adorned with <s>sāgaravaramaṇi</s> (ocean-best) jewels, surpassing the divine, hung with golden threads, adorned with necklaces of <s>rucaka</s> (ornamental) jewels, pearl necklaces, blue pearl necklaces, <s>siṃhalatā</s> (lion-vine) girdles, strands of jewel-threads and all manner of jeweled ornaments, spread with nets of gold, pearl nets, and nets of all jewels with tinkling bells, adorned with <s>makara</s>, <s>svastika</s>, <s>nandyāvarta</s>, and crescent-moon motifs, decorated with nets of jeweled bells, golden ornaments of all jewels. It is adorned to please beings according to their aspirations. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, the sound and proclamation that issues forth from that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s> when stirred by the wind pervades immeasurable world-realms. For those beings, <s>Ānanda</s>, whose ears perceive that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s>, no ear-disease is to be anticipated up until the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening). For those immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, boundless, and inexpressible beings whose eyes perceive that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s>, no eye-disease is to be anticipated up until the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, for those beings who smell the fragrance from that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s>, no nose-disease is to be anticipated up until the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>. For those beings who taste the fruits of that <s>bodhivṛkṣa</s>, no tongue-disease is to be anticipated up until the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>. For those beings who are touched by the rays emitted from (

children.text: START Sukhv 33:
children.translated_text: [Section 33:]

children.text: tatraiva khalu punarānanda ye bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ pratyājāyante pratyājaniṣyante vā, sarve te ekajātipratibaddhāstata evānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante sthāpayitvā praṇidhānavaśaṃ ye te bodhisattvā mahāsiṃhanādanādina udārasaṃnāhasaṃnaddhāḥ sarvasattvaparinirvāṇābhiyuktāśca || Sukhv_33 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been born, are being born, or will be born in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) — all of them are bound by a single birth remaining before attaining the supreme, perfect awakening from that very place, setting aside those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who, armored with the great lion's roar and endowed with noble resolution, are devoted to the complete liberation of all beings through the power of their vows.

children.text: START Sukhv 34:
children.translated_text: [Section 34:]

children.text: tasmina khalu punarānanda buddhakṣetre ye śrāvakānte vyāmaprabhāḥ, te bodhisattvāste yojanakoṭīśatasahasraprabhāḥ, sthāpayitvā dvau bodhisattvau yayoḥ prabhayā sā lokadhātuḥ satatasamitaṃ nityāvabhāsasphuṭā | atha khalvāyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - kiṃnāmadheyau bhagavaṃstau bodhisattvau mahāsattvau? bhagavānāha - ekastayorānanda avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ dvitīyo mahāsthāmaprāpto nāma | ita eva cānanda buddhakṣetrāccyutā tau tatropapannau || Sukhv_34 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) have a radiance extending one <s>vyāma</s> (fathom), while the <s>bodhisattvas</s> have a radiance extending hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yojanas</s>, setting aside two <s>bodhisattvas</s> by whose radiance that entire world-realm is constantly and perpetually illuminated. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: "What are the names, Blessed One, of those two <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings)?" The Blessed One replied: "One of them, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, and the second is named <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>. It was from this very <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, that they passed away and were reborn there."

children.text: START Sukhv 35:
children.translated_text: [Section 35:]

children.text: tatra cānanda buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ, sarve te dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇasamanvāgatāḥ paripūrṇagātrā dhyānābhijñākovidāḥ prajñāprabhedakuśalāstīkṣṇendriyāḥ susaṃvṛtendriyā ājñātāvīndriyā adīnābalendriyāḥ pratilambhakṣāntikā anantāparyantaguṇāḥ || Sukhv_35 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, all the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been born in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> are endowed with the thirty-two marks of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being), with fully developed bodies, skilled in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>abhijñā</s> (supernatural knowledge), proficient in the distinctions of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), of sharp faculties, well-restrained in their faculties, possessing the faculty of final knowledge, of undiminished faculties of power, endowed with the patience of attainment, of infinite and boundless virtues.

children.text: START Sukhv 36:
children.translated_text: [Section 36:]

children.text: tasmin khalu punarānanda buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvā pratyājātāḥ, sarve te 'virahitā buddhadarśanenāvinipātadharmāṇo yāvadbodhiparyantam | sarve te tata upādāya na jātu jātismarā bhaviṣyanti sthāpayitvā tathārūpeṣu kalpasaṃkṣobheṣu ye pūrvasthānapraṇihitāḥ pañcasu kaṣāyeṣu vartamāneṣu yadā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati tadyathāpi nāma mamaitarhi || Sukhv_36 ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, all the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been born in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> are never separated from the sight of <s>Buddhas</s>, and they are of the nature of non-regression up until the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>. All of them from that point onward will never lose the recollection of past births, setting aside those who, during such upheavals of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), have been stationed at former posts when the five defilements are prevalent and the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, arise in the world — just as it is with me now.

children.text: START Sukhv 37:
children.translated_text: [Section 37:]

children.text: tasmin khalu punarānanda buddhakṣetre ye bodhisattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ, sarve te ekapurobhaktenānyāṃllokadhātūn gatvā anekāni buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyupatiṣṭhanti yāvadākāṅkṣanti buddhānubhāvena | te yathā yathā cittamutpādayanti evamevaṃrūpaiḥ puṣpadhūpadīpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantītūryasaṃgītivādyaiḥ pūjāṃ kuryāma iti, teṣāṃ sahacittotpādāttathārūpāṇi ca sarvapūjāvidhānāni pāṇau prādurbhavanti | te taiḥ puṣpairyāvadvādyaisteṣu buddheṣu bhagavatsu pūjāṃ kurvanto bahvaparimāṇāsaṃkhyeyaṃ kuśalamupacinvanti | sacetpunarākāṅkṣanti evaṃrūpāḥ puṣpapuṭāḥ pāṇau prādurbhavantviti, teṣāṃ sahacittotpādānnānāvarṇā anekavarṇā nānāgandhā divyāḥ puṣpapuṭāḥ pāṇau prādurbhavanti | te taistathārūpaiḥ puṣpapuṭaistān buddhān bhagavato 'vakiranti abhyavakiranti abhiprakiranti | teṣāṃ ca yaḥ sarvaparītaḥ puṣpapuṭa (
Sukhv, Vaidya 246
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 246]

children.text: ) utsṛṣṭaḥ sa daśayojanavistaraṃ puṣpacchatraṃ prādurbhavati uparyantarīkṣe | dvitīye cānutsṛṣṭe na prathamo dharaṇyāṃ prapatati | santi tatra puṣpapuṭā ya utsṛṣṭāḥ santo viṃśatiyojanavistārāṇi puṣpacchatrāṇyuparyantarīkṣe prādurbhavanti | santi triṃśaccatvāriṃśatpañcāśadyojanavistārāṇi, santi yāvadyojanaśatasahasravistārāṇi puṣpacchatrāṇyuparyantarīkṣe prādurbhavanti | tatra ye udāraṃ prītiprāmodyaṃ saṃjanayanti, udāraṃ ca cittaudvilyaṃ pratilabhante, te bahvaparimitamasaṃkhyeyaṃ kuśalamūlamavaropya bahūni ca buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyupasthāya ekapūrvāhṇena punarapi sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau pratiṣṭhante tasyaivāmitāyuṣastathāgatasya pūrvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānaparigraheṇa pūrvadattadharmaśravaṇena pūrvajināvaropitakuśalamūlatayā pūrvapraṇidhānasamṛddhiparipūryātmabhūtayā suvibhaktabhāvitayā || Sukhv_37 ||
children.translated_text: When released, it manifests as a flower canopy ten <s>yojanas</s> in extent up in the sky. When the second has not yet been released, the first does not fall to the ground. There are flower buds which, when released, manifest as flower canopies twenty <s>yojanas</s> in extent up in the sky. Some are thirty, forty, or fifty <s>yojanas</s> in extent; some manifest as flower canopies up to a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent up in the sky. Those who generate noble joy and delight, and attain noble elation of mind, having planted immeasurable and incalculable roots of merit and having attended upon many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, in a single forenoon they again become established in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, through the sustaining power of the former vow of that very <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, through the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> previously given, through having roots of merit planted by former <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), through the fulfillment and completion of former vows in their own being, and through well-distinguished cultivation. [Sukhv 37]

Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, all the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been born in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> go, within a single morning meal, to other world-realms and attend upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> for as long as they wish, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>. According to the intention they generate — 'With offerings of such and such a form — flowers, incense, lamps, fragrances, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, victory-standards, musical performances and concerts — may we make offerings' — at the very moment of their intention, such offerings appear in their hands. With those flowers and instruments they make offerings to those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, and accumulate vast, immeasurable, incalculable merit. And if they further wish, 'Let such flower-baskets appear in our hands,' at the very moment of their intention, flower-baskets of various colors, many hues, and various divine fragrances appear in their hands. With those flower-baskets they shower, cover, and scatter offerings upon those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones. And whatever shower of flower-baskets is scattered all around (

children.text: START Sukhv 38:
children.translated_text: [Section 38:]

children.text: tasmin khalu punarānanda buddhakṣetre ye sattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ, sarve te sarvajñatāsahagatāmeva dharmakathāṃ kathayanti | na ca tatra buddhakṣetre sattvānāṃ kācitparigrahasaṃjñāsti | te sarve ca tadbuddhakṣetramanucaṃkramamāṇā anuvicaranto na ratiṃ nāratimutpādayanti | prakrāmantaścānapekṣāḥ, na ca prakrāmanti sāpekṣāḥ | sarvasattveṣāmeva cittaṃ nāsti | tatra khalu punarānanda sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau ye sattvāḥ pratyājātāḥ, nāsti teṣāmanyatamakasaṃjñā, nāsti svakasaṃjñā, nāstyasamasaṃjñā, nāsti vigrahaḥ,nāsti vivādaḥ,nāsti virodhaḥ | samacittā maitracittā mṛducittāḥ snigdhacittāḥ karmaṇyacittāḥ prasannacittāḥ sthiracittā vinīvaraṇacittā akṣubhitacittā alulitacittāḥ prajñāpāramitācaryācaraṇacittāścittādhārabuddhipraviṣṭāḥ | sāgarasamāḥ prajñayā,merusamā buddhyā, anekaguṇasaṃnicayāḥ, bodhyaṅgasaṃgītyā vikrīḍitāḥ, buddhasaṃgītyabhiyuktā māṃsacakṣuḥ pravicinvanti, divyaṃ cakṣurabhinirharanti, prajñācakṣurgatiṃgatā dharmacakṣuḥpāragatā buddhacakṣurniṣpādayanto darśayanto dyotayanto vistareṇa prakāśayanto 'saṅgajñānamabhinirharanti | traidhātukasamatāyāmabhiyuktā dāntacittāḥ śāntacittāḥ sarvadharmadhātūpalabdhisamanvāgatāḥ samudayaniruktikuśalā dharmaniruktisamanvāgatā hārāhārakuśalā nayānayakuśalāḥ sthānakuśalā laukikīṣu kathāsvanapekṣā viharanti | lokottarābhiḥ kathābhiḥ sāraṃ pratyayanti | sarvadharmaparyeṣṭikuśalāḥ sarvadharmaprakṛtivyupaśamajñānavihāriṇo 'nupalambhagocarā niṣkiṃcanā nirupādānā niścintā nirupadhayo 'nupādāya suvimuktā anaṅgaṇā aparyasthāyino 'bhijñāsu amūlasthāyino 'saṅgācārikā anavalīnā gambhīreṣu dharmeṣvabhiyuktā na saṃsīdanti dūranubodhabuddhajñānapraveśodgatā ekāyanamārgānuprāptā nirvicikitsāstīrṇakathaṃkathā aparapratyayajñānā anadhimāninaḥ | sumerusamā jñānābhyudgatāḥ | sāgarasamā buddhyakṣobhyāḥ | candrasūryaprabhātikrāntāḥ prajñābhayā pāṇḍarasuśuklaśuddhaśubhacittatayā ca | uttaptahemavarṇasadṛśā avabhāsanirbhāsatayā ca | vasuṃdharāsadṛśāḥ sarvasattvaśubhāśubhakṣamaṇatayā | apsadṛśāḥ sarvakleśamūlanirdhāvanapravāhaṇatayā ca | agnirājasadṛśāḥ sarvadharmamanyanākleśanirdahanatayā | vāyusadṛśāḥ sarvalokāsañjanatayā | ākāśasadṛśāḥ sarvadharmanairvedhikatayā sarvaśo niṣkiṃcanatayā ca | (
Sukhv, Vaidya 247
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 247]

children.text: ) padmasadṛśāḥ sarvalokānupaliptatayā | kālānusārimahāmeghasadṛśā dharmābhigarjanatayā | mahāvṛṣṭisadṛśā dharmasalilābhipravarṣaṇatayā | ṛṣabhasadṛśā mahāgaṇābhibhavanatayā | mahānāgasadṛśāḥ paramasudāntacittatayā | bhadrāśvājāneyasadṛśāḥ suvinītatayā | siṃhamṛgarājasadṛśā vikramavaiśāradyāsaṃtrastatayā | nyagrodhadrumarājasadṛśāḥ sarvasattvaparitrāṇatayā | parvatarājasadṛśāḥ sarvaparapravādyakampanatayā | gaganasadṛśā aparimāṇamaitrīprabhāvanatayā | mahābrahmasamāḥ sarvakuśalamūladharmādhipatyapūrvaṃgamatayā | pakṣisadṛśā asaṃnicayasthānatayā | garuḍadvijarājasadṛśāḥ sarvaparapravādividhvaṃsanatayā | udumbarapuṣpasadṛśā durlabhāpratyarthitayā | nāgavatsusamāhitā avikṣiptājihmendriyatayā | viniścayakuśalāḥ kṣāntisaurabhyabahulāḥ | anīrṣukāḥ parasaṃpattyaprārthanatayā | viśāradā dharmakathā svatṛptā dharmaparyeṣṭayā | vaiḍūryasadṛśāḥ śīlena | ratnākarāḥ śrutena | mañjusvarā mahādharmadundubhinirghoṣeṇa | mahādharmabherīṃ parāghnanto mahādharmaśaṅkhamāpūrayanto mahādharmadhvajamucchrāpayanto dharmolkāṃ prajvālayantaḥ prajñāvilokino 'saṃmūḍhā nirdoṣāḥ śāntakhilāḥ śuddhā nirāmagandhā alubdhāḥ saṃvibhāgaratā muktatyāgāḥ prasṛtapāṇayo dānasaṃvibhāgaratā dharmāmiṣābhyāṃ dāne 'matsariṇo 'saṃsṛṣṭā urtrastamānasā viraktā dhīrā dhaureyā dhṛtimanto hrīmantaḥ suvyūḍhasattvā nirgāḍhāḥ prāptābhijñāḥ suratāḥ sukhasaṃvāsā arthakarā lokapradyotā nāpadāgantuṃ dhīrā rāgaṃ tamaḥ pranekasvaṣṭhaḥ(?) śokāpagatā nirmalā nimeṣaprahīṇā vikrīḍitābhijñā hetubalikāḥ praṇidhānabalikā ajihmā akuṭilā ete lakṣakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlā utpāṭitamānaśalyā apagatarāgadveṣamohāḥ śuddhāḥ śuddhādhimuktā jinabalapraśastā lokapaṇḍitā uttaptajñānasamudāgatā jinasutāścittaudbilyasamanvāgatāḥ śūrā dṛḍhā amamā akhilā atulā arajaskāḥ sahitā udārā ṛṣabhā hrīmanto dhṛtimantaḥ smṛtimanto matimanto gatimantaḥ prajñāśastrapraharaṇā puṇyavanto dyutimanto vyapagatakhilā malaprahīṇāḥ smṛtiyuktāḥ śāntajñānālambhāḥ | īdṛśā ānanda tasmin buddhakṣetre sattvāḥ saṃkṣiptena ca | vistareṇa punaḥ sacetkalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasthitikenāpyāyuṣpramāṇena tathāgatā nirdiśyeran,naiva śakyaṃ teṣāṃ satpuruṣāṇāṃ guṇaparyantamadhigantum, na ca tathāgatasya vaiśāradyopacchedo bhavet | tatkasya hetoḥ? ubhayamapyeva ānanda acintyamatulyaṃ yadidaṃ teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ guṇāstathāgatasya cānuttaraprajñāpratibhānam || Sukhv_38 ||
children.translated_text: Like lotuses, through being unstained by all worlds; like great clouds that follow the seasons, through thundering forth the <s>Dharma</s>; like great rain, through showering the water of <s>Dharma</s>; like bulls, through surpassing great assemblies; like great elephants, through having supremely well-tamed minds; like noble thoroughbred horses, through being well-trained; like lions, kings of beasts, through fearlessness in valor and confidence; like <s>nyagrodha</s> trees, kings of trees, through sheltering all beings; like mountain kings, through being unshaken by all opposing doctrines; like the sky, through the power of immeasurable <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness); equal to great <s>Brahmā</s>, through taking the lead in sovereignty over all roots of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; like birds, through not abiding in accumulation; like <s>garuḍas</s>, kings of birds, through destroying all opposing doctrines; like <s>udumbara</s> flowers, through being rare and unsought; well-concentrated like <s>nāgas</s>, through having undistracted and upright faculties; skilled in discernment, rich in the fragrance of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience); without envy, through not desiring the fortune of others; confident in <s>Dharma</s> discourse, self-satisfied in their investigation of the <s>Dharma</s>; like <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) in moral conduct; treasure mines in learning; with melodious voices through the sound of the great <s>Dharma</s> drum — striking the great <s>Dharma</s> kettledrum, filling the great <s>Dharma</s> conch, raising the great <s>Dharma</s> banner, kindling the <s>Dharma</s> torch, with wisdom-vision, unconfused, faultless, with hostility pacified, pure, without taint or odor, ungreedy, delighting in sharing, generous in giving, with hands extended delighting in giving and sharing, not selfish in giving both <s>Dharma</s> and material gifts, unentangled, with minds turned away [from the world], dispassionate, steadfast, patient, resolute, conscientious, with well-marshaled courage, deeply entered, having attained the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), joyful, pleasant to live with, helpful, illuminators of the world, unable to be overtaken by calamity, steadfast — having eliminated passion, darkness, and grief, stainless, with blinking eliminated, delighting in the <s>abhijñās</s>, strong in causes, strong in vows, upright, not crooked — these <s>bodhisattvas</s> have roots of merit planted through <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>lakṣas</s>; they have extracted the thorn of pride, are free from passion, hatred, and delusion, pure, with pure resolve, sons of the Victorious Ones, praised by the power of the Victorious Ones, wise ones of the world, with refined knowledge arisen, sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, endowed with elation of mind, heroic, firm, selfless, without hostility, incomparable, dustless, united, noble, bull-like, conscientious, resolute, mindful, intelligent, with progress, with wisdom as their weapon, meritorious, radiant, with hostility departed, with impurities abandoned, endowed with mindfulness, resting in peaceful knowledge. Such, <s>Ānanda</s>, in brief, are the beings in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. And in detail, even if the <s>Tathāgatas</s> were to describe them with a lifespan lasting <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, they could not reach the limit of those good beings' virtues, nor would there be any diminution of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s eloquence. For what reason? Both are inconceivable and incomparable, <s>Ānanda</s> — namely, the virtues of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and the unsurpassed wisdom and eloquence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. [Sukhv 38]

Moreover, <s>Ānanda</s>, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), all the beings who have been reborn speak only <s>Dharma</s> discourses accompanied by <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). In that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, beings have no notion of possession whatsoever. All of them, walking about and wandering through that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, generate neither attachment nor aversion. They proceed without longing, and do not proceed with longing. There is no discriminating mind among all beings. Moreover, <s>Ānanda</s>, among the beings reborn in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, there is no notion of otherness, no notion of self, no notion of inequality; there is no dispute, no quarrel, no conflict. They are of equal mind, benevolent mind, gentle mind, affectionate mind, pliable mind, serene mind, stable mind, unobstructed mind, undisturbed mind, unagitated mind; their minds practice the conduct of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) and have entered the foundation of wisdom-mind. Equal to the ocean in wisdom, equal to <s>Meru</s> in intelligence, possessing an accumulation of manifold virtues, delighting in the harmony of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), devoted to the harmony of the <s>Buddhas</s>, they discern with the fleshly eye, bring forth the divine eye, have attained the course of the wisdom eye, have reached the far shore of the <s>Dharma</s> eye, perfecting, displaying, illuminating, and extensively revealing the <s>Buddha</s> eye — they bring forth unattached knowledge. Devoted to the equality of the three realms, with tamed and peaceful minds, endowed with the attainment of the realm of all <s>dharmas</s>, skilled in the analysis of arising, endowed with the analysis of <s>dharmas</s>, skilled in what to accept and what to reject, skilled in proper and improper methods, skilled in occasions — they dwell without interest in worldly conversations. They find the essence in transcendent conversations. Skilled in the investigation of all <s>dharmas</s>, abiding in the knowledge of the natural quiescence of all <s>dharmas</s>, whose sphere is non-apprehension, possessionless, without clinging, without worry, without substrata, well-liberated without grasping, stainless, not settled down, established in the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) without being rooted in anything, wandering without attachment, not shrinking back, devoted to profound <s>dharmas</s> — they do not sink. Having entered the lofty, hard-to-fathom <s>Buddha</s> knowledge, having attained the one-way path, free from doubt, having crossed over uncertainty, with knowledge independent of others, without overestimation —

children.text: START Sukhv 39:
children.translated_text: [Section 39:]

children.text: api cānanda uttiṣṭha, paścānmukhībhūtvā puṣpāvakīrṇāñjalīṃ pragṛhya praṇipata | eṣā sā dig yatra sa bhagavānamitābhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati, dharmaṃ ca deśayati virajo viśuddhaṃ yasya tannāmadheyamanāvaraṇe daśadiśi loke vighuṣṭam ekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā buddhā bhagavanto varṇayanti stuvanti praśaṃsantyasakṛdasakṛdasaṅgavācāprativākyāḥ | evamukte āyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - icchāmyahaṃ bhagavaṃstamamitābhamamitaprabhamamitāyuṣaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ draṣṭum, tāṃśca bodhisattvān mahāsattvān bahubuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlān | samanantarabhāṣitā āyuṣmatānandeneyaṃ (
Sukhv, Vaidya 248
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 248]

children.text: ) vāk, atha tāvadeva so 'mitābhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ svapāṇitalāttathārūpaṃ raśmiṃ prāmuñcadyadidaṃ koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ mahatāvabhāsena sphuṭamabhūt | tena khalu punaḥ samayena sarvatra koṭīśatasahasrabuddhakṣetrāṇāṃ ye kecitkālaparvatā vā ratnaparvatā vā merumahāmerumucilindamahāmucilindacakravālamahācakravālā vā citayo vā stambhā vā vṛkṣagahanodyānavimānāni divyamanuṣyakāṇi, tāni sarvāṇi tasya tathāgatasya tayā prabhayābhinirbhinnānyabhūvan samabhibhūtāni | tadyathāpi nāma puruṣo vyāmamātrake 'nvito dvitīyaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyavekṣedāditye 'bhyudgate, evamevāsmin buddhakṣetre bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikādevanāgayakṣarākṣasagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāśca tasyāṃ velāyāmadrākṣustamamitābhaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ sumerumiva parvatarājaṃ sarvakṣetrābhyudgataṃ sarvā diśo 'bhibhūya bhāsamānaṃ tapantaṃ virocamānaṃ vibhrājamānam, taṃ ca mahāntaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ taṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ yadidaṃ buddhānubhāvena tasyāḥ prabhāyāḥ pariśuddhatvāt | tadyatheyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ekodakajātā bhavet, tatra na vṛkṣā na parvatā na dvīpā na tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayo na nadīśvabhraprapātāḥ prajñāpayeran, anyatraikārṇavībhūtā mahāpṛthivyekā syāt, evameva tasmin buddhakṣetre nāstyanyatkiṃcilliṅgaṃ vā nimittaṃ vā anyatraiva vyāmaprabhāḥ śrāvakāste ca yojanakoṭīśatasahasraprabhā bodhisattvāḥ | sa ca bhagavānamitābhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastaṃ ca śrāvakagaṇaṃ taṃ ca bodhisattvagaṇamabhibhūya sarvā diśaḥ prabhāsayan saṃdṛśyate | tena khalvapi samayena tasyāṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau bodhisattvāḥ śrāvakadevamanuṣyāśca sarve te imāḥ sahālokadhātuṃ śākyamuniṃ ca tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamarhatā bhikṣusaṃghena parivṛtaṃ paśyanti sma dharmaṃ deśayantam || Sukhv_39 ||
children.translated_text: speech. Then at that very moment, that <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly and Fully Awakened One, released from his own palm such a ray of light that this hundred-thousand-<s>koṭī-niyuta</s>-th <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) became manifest with great radiance. At that time, throughout all the hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, whatever dark mountains, jewel mountains, <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mahāmeru</s>, <s>Mucilinda</s> and <s>Mahāmucilinda</s>, <s>Cakravāla</s> and <s>Mahācakravāla</s> mountains, mounds, pillars, tree-groves, gardens, and celestial and human palaces there were — all of these were pierced through and overcome by that radiance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Just as a person standing within a fathom's reach might look upon a second person when the sun has risen, even so in this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans — at that moment they beheld that <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly and Fully Awakened One, like <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, towering above all fields, shining, blazing, glowing, and resplendent in all directions, together with that great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and that community of monks — all this by the power of the <s>Buddha</s> and by the purity of that radiance. Just as this great earth might become one mass of water, where no trees, no mountains, no islands, no grasses, shrubs, herbs, or forest trees, no rivers, chasms, or waterfalls could be discerned — nothing but one great ocean, one single earth — even so in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> there was no other mark or sign whatsoever, except only the fathom-radiant <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and the <s>bodhisattvas</s> with radiance extending a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yojanas</s>. And that Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly and Fully Awakened One, surpassing both the assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s> and the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, was seen illuminating all directions with his radiance. At that very time, in that world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>śrāvakas</s>, gods, and humans — all of them beheld this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm and <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly and Fully Awakened One, surrounded by a venerable community of monks, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. || Sukhv_39 ||

Moreover, <s>Ānanda</s>, rise up, face westward, join your hands filled with scattered flowers, and bow down. This is the direction where that <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) <s>Amitābha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwells, abides, and lives, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, pure and stainless, whose name resounds throughout the unobstructed world in all ten directions. In each direction, <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavants</s>, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, praise, laud, and extol him again and again with unhindered speech and unanswered words. Thus addressed, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I wish, <s>Bhagavān</s>, to see that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Amitaprabha</s> (Immeasurable Light), <s>Amitāyus</s> (Immeasurable Life), the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and those <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> who have planted roots of merit through many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>.' Immediately upon this being spoken by the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, this —

children.text: tatra khalu bhagavānajitaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma - paśyasi tvamajita amuṣmina buddhakṣetre guṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadam? upariṣṭāccāntarīkṣe ārāmaramaṇīyānyudyānaramaṇīyāni nadīpuṣkariṇīramaṇīyāni nānāratnapadmotpalakumudapuṇḍarīkākīrṇāni? adhastācca dharaṇītalamupādāya yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanādgaganatalaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇaṃ puṣpāvalisamupaśobhitaṃ nānāratnastambapaṅktiparisphuṭaṃ tathāgatābhinirmitanānādvijasaṃghaniṣevitam? ajito bodhisattva āha - paśyāmi bhagavan | bhagavānāha - paśyasi punastvamajita etānamarān dvijasaṃghān sarvabuddhakṣetraṃ buddhasvareṇābhivijñāpayantaṃ yenaite bodhisattvā nityamavirahitā buddhānusmṛtyā? ajita āha - paśyāmi bhagavan | bhagavānāha - paśyasi punastvamajita atra buddhakṣetre 'mūn sattvān yojanaśatasahasrikeṣu vimāneṣvabhirūḍhānantarīkṣe sasatkārān krāmantaḥ? ajita āha - paśyāmi bhagavan | bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase ajita asti kiṃcinnānātvaṃ devānāṃ paranirmitavaśavartināṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau manuṣyāṇāṃ vā? ajita āha - ekamapyahaṃ bhagavan nānātvaṃ na samanupaśyāmi yāvanmaharddhikā atra sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau manuṣyāḥ | bhagavānāha - paśyasi punastvamajita tatra sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāveteṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāmudāreṣu padmeṣu garbhāvāsam? āha - tadyathāpi nāma devāstrāyastriṃśā devā yāmā vā pañcāśadyojanikeṣu vā (
Sukhv, Sukhv, Vaidya 249
children.translated_text: [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, <s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, Vaidya edition, p. 249]

children.text: ) yojanaśatikeṣu vā pañcayojanaśatikeṣu vā vimāneṣu praviṣṭāḥ krīḍanti ramanti paricārayanti, evamevāhaṃ bhagavan atra sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāveteṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāmudāreṣu padmeṣu garbhāvāsaṃ paśyāmi || Sukhv_40 ||
children.translated_text: palaces of a hundred <s>yojanas</s> or five hundred <s>yojanas</s>, even so, Blessed One, I see in this world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> the womb-abode of those humans within great lotuses. || Sukhv_40 ||

Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Ajita</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> thus: "Do you see, <s>Ajita</s>, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> the splendid array of excellent qualities? Above, in the sky, delightful gardens, delightful parks, delightful rivers, and lotus pools filled with various jeweled lotuses, <s>utpalas</s> (blue lotuses), <s>kumudas</s> (night-lotuses), and <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> (white lotuses)? And below, from the surface of the earth up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens and the expanse of the sky, strewn with flowers, adorned with garlands of flowers, resplendent with rows of various jeweled pillars, frequented by flocks of various birds created by the <s>Tathāgata</s>?" <s>Ajita</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> replied: "I see it, Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "Do you further see, <s>Ajita</s>, these immortal flocks of birds proclaiming the sound of the <s>Buddha</s> throughout the entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, so that these <s>bodhisattvas</s> are never separated from the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>?" <s>Ajita</s> replied: "I see it, Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "Do you further see, <s>Ajita</s>, in this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> those beings who have ascended palaces of a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues), traversing the sky with reverence?" <s>Ajita</s> replied: "I see it, Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Ajita</s> — is there any difference between the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods and the humans in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>?" <s>Ajita</s> replied: "I do not perceive even a single difference, Blessed One — so great is the supernatural power of the humans here in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>." The Blessed One said: "Do you further see, <s>Ajita</s>, in that world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, the womb-abode of those humans within great lotuses?" He replied: "Just as, for example, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods or the <s>Yāma</s> gods enter and sport and delight and enjoy themselves in palaces of fifty <s>yojanas</s> or

children.text: santi khalu punaratra bhagavan sattvā ya aupapādukāḥ padmeṣu paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhavanti | tatko 'tra bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yadanye garbhāvāsaṃ prativasanti, anye punaraupapādukāḥ padmeṣu paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhavanti? bhagavānāha - ye te ajita bodhisattvā anyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu sthitāḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapattaye vicikitsāmutpādayanti, tena cittena kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti, teṣāmatra garbhāvāso bhavati | ye punarnirvicikitsāmutpādya cchinnakāṅkṣāḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapattaye kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti, buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmasaṅgajñānamevākalpayanti abhiśraddadhati adhimucyante,te aupapādukāḥ padmeṣu paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhavanti | ye te ajita bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anyatra buddhakṣetreṣu sthitāścittamutpādayanti amitābhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya darśanāya, na vicikitsāmutpādayanti, na kāṅkṣanti asaṅgaṃ buddhajñānam, svakuśalamūlaṃ cābhiśraddadhati, teṣāmaupapādukānāṃ paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhūtānāṃ muhūrtamātreṇa evaṃrūpaḥ kāyo bhavati tadyathānyeṣāṃ ciropapannānāṃ sattvānām | paśya ajita prajñāviśeṣaṃ prajñāvaimātryaṃ prajñāparihāṇiṃ prajñāparīttatām - yattu hitāya pañcavarṣaśatāni parihīṇā bhavanti buddhadarśanādbodhisattvadarśanāddharmaśravaṇāddharmasaṃkathanāt | kuśalamūlacaryāyāḥ parihīṇā bhavanti sarvakuśalamūlasaṃpattibhiḥ yadidaṃ vicikitsāpatitaiḥ saṃjñāmanasikāraiḥ | tadyathāpi nāma ajita rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya bandhanāgāraṃ bhavetsarvasauvarṇavaiḍūryapratyuptamavasaktapaṭṭamālyadāmakalāpaṃ nānāraṅgavibhavavitānaṃ dūṣyapaṭṭasaṃchannaṃ nānāpuṣpakusumābhikīrṇamudāradhūpanirdhūpitaṃ prāsādaharmyaniryūhagavākṣavedikātoraṇavicitraṃ saptaratnaṃ kiṅkiṇījālasaṃchannaṃ caturasraṃ catuḥsthūṇaṃ caturdvāraṃ catuḥsopānam | tatra tasya sa rājñaḥ putraḥ kenacideva kṛtyena prakṣipya jāmbūnadasuvarṇamayairnigaḍairbaddho bhavati | tasya ca tatra paryaṅkaḥ prajñaptaḥ syādanekagoṇikāstīrṇastūlikāparṇakāstīrṇaḥ kāliṅgaprāvaraṇapratyāstaraṇasottarapadacchada ubhayāntalohitopadhānaścitro darśanīyaḥ | sa tatra tadābhiṣaṇṇo vā abhisaṃpanno vā bhavet | bahu cāsyānekavidhaṃ śuci vinītaṃ pānabhojanaṃ tatropanāmyeta | tatkiṃ manyase ajita udārastasya rājaputrasya sa paribhogo bhavet? ajita āha - udāro bhagavan | bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase ajita api tvāsvādayettatra niśāmayecca,tena vā tuṣṭiṃ vidyāt?āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | api tu khalu punaryadyapanītya rājñā tatra bandhanāgāre prakṣipto bhavet,sa tato mokṣamevākāṅkṣet | abhijātān kumārānamātyān stryāgārān śreṣṭhino gṛhapatīn koṭṭarājāṃśca paryeṣayet, ya enaṃ tato bandhanāgārātparimocayeyuḥ | kiṃcāpi bhagavaṃstasya rājakumārasya tatra bandhānāgāre nābhiratiḥ, nātra parimucyate, yāvanna rājā prasādamupadarśayati | bhagavānāha - evameva ajita ye te bodhisattvā vicikitsāpatitāḥ kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti, (

children.text: ) kāṅkṣati buddhajñānam, kiṃcāpi tena buddhanāmaśravaṇena tena ca cittaprasādamātreṇa atra sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapadyante, na tu khalvaupapādukāḥ padmeṣu paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhavanti, api tu padmeṣu garbhāvāsaṃ prativasanti | kiṃcāpi teṣāṃ tatrodyānavimānasaṃjñāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante, nāstyuccāraprasrāvam, nāsti kheṭasiṃhāṇakam, na pratikūlaṃ manasaḥ pravartate, api tu khalu punaḥ pañca varṣaśatāni virahitā bhavanti buddhadarśanena dharmaśravaṇena bodhisattvadarśanena dharmasāṃkathyaviniścayena sarvakuśalamūlena dharmacaryābhiśca | kiṃcāpi te tatra nābhiramante na tuṣṭiṃ vijānanti,api tu khalu punaḥ pūrvāparān kṣapayitsate bhūyastataḥ paścānniskrāmanti | na caiṣāṃ tato niṣkrāmatāṃ niṣkramaḥ prajñāyate ūrdhvamadhastiryagvā | paśya ajita etarhi nāma pañcabhirvarṣaśatairbahūni buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasropasthānāni syurbahvaparimāṇāsaṃkhyeyāprameyāṇi ca kuśalamūlānyavaropayitavyāni | tatsarvaṃ vicikitsādoṣeṇa vināśayanti | paśya ajita kiyanmahate 'narthāya bodhisattvānāṃ vicikitsā saṃvartata iti | tasmāttarhi ajita bodhisattvairnirvicikitsairbodhaye cittamutpādya kṣipraṃ sarvasattvahitasukhādhānāya sāmarthyapratilambhārthaṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapattaye kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayitavyāni, yatra bhagavānamitābhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ || Sukhv_41 ||
children.translated_text: ) doubts the <s>buddhajñāna</s> (Buddha-knowledge)—although through merely hearing the Buddha's name and through mere faith of mind they are born here in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, they do not appear miraculously on lotuses in cross-legged posture, but rather dwell in a womb-like enclosure within the lotuses. Although perceptions of gardens and palaces arise for them there, there is no excrement or urine, no phlegm or mucus, and nothing disagreeable arises in their minds; yet for five hundred years they are deprived of seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, seeing <s>bodhisattvas</s>, conversing about and ascertaining the <s>Dharma</s>, of all roots of merit, and of <s>Dharma</s>-practices. Although they do not delight there and find no contentment, yet they pass through their former and latter periods and eventually emerge. But when they emerge from there, their emergence is not perceived as upward, downward, or sideways. See, <s>Ajita</s>, in those five hundred years they could have served many <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> and planted immeasurable, incalculable, and innumerable roots of merit. All of that they destroy through the fault of doubt. See, <s>Ajita</s>, how great a disadvantage doubt brings to <s>bodhisattvas</s>! Therefore, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> should generate the mind for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) without doubt, and should dedicate their roots of merit for birth in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, in order to quickly attain the power to establish the welfare and happiness of all beings, where the Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One dwells. [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> 41]

"There are indeed, Blessed One, beings here who are born spontaneously, appearing cross-legged upon lotuses. What, Blessed One, is the cause and condition that some dwell in womb-abodes while others appear spontaneously, cross-legged upon lotuses?" The Blessed One replied: "Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, who, while dwelling in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, generate doubt regarding rebirth in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> and with that mind plant roots of merit — for them there is a womb-abode here. But those who, having abandoned doubt and being free from hesitation, plant roots of merit for rebirth in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, who conceive of nothing but the unattached knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, who have faith and devotion — they appear spontaneously, cross-legged upon lotuses. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, who, while dwelling in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, generate the aspiration to see the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly and Fully Awakened One, who do not generate doubt, who do not hesitate regarding the unattached <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, and who have faith in their own roots of merit — for them, being born spontaneously and appearing cross-legged, in a mere moment their bodies become such as those of other beings who have been reborn there long ago. Behold, <s>Ajita</s>, the distinction of wisdom, the measure of wisdom, the decline of wisdom, the diminishment of wisdom — that for five hundred years they are deprived of seeing <s>Buddhas</s>, seeing <s>bodhisattvas</s>, hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and conversing about the <s>Dharma</s>, all for their own benefit. They are deprived of all the attainments of roots of merit — this through perceptions and mental activities beset by doubt. Just as, <s>Ajita</s>, a king, a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior) consecrated upon the head, might have a prison made entirely of gold and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), adorned with garlands and festoons of cloth and flowers, with canopies of various colors and splendors, couches spread with silken and cotton covers, strewn with various flowers and blossoms, perfumed with fine incense, adorned with terraces, towers, turrets, windows, railings, and gateways — made of the seven jewels, covered with nets of tinkling bells, four-cornered, four-pillared, with four doors and four staircases. There, the king's son, for some offense, might be cast in and bound with fetters of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold. And a couch might be prepared for him there, spread with many cushions and mattresses, with coverings of <s>Kāliṅga</s> cloth and fine spreads, with red pillows on both sides — beautiful and lovely to behold. And he might sit upon it or recline upon it. And much pure and refined food and drink, various and abundant, might be offered to him there. What do you think, <s>Ajita</s> — would that prince's enjoyment be splendid?" <s>Ajita</s> replied: "It would be splendid, Blessed One." The Blessed One said: "What do you think, <s>Ajita</s> — would he savor and enjoy it there, or would he find contentment in it?" He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. Rather, if that prince were cast into that prison by the king, he would only long for release from it. He would seek out noble youths, ministers, ladies of the harem, merchants, householders, and vassal kings who might free him from that prison. Moreover, Blessed One, even though the prince in that prison has no delight, he is not released from it until the king shows him favor." children.text: evamukte ajito bodhisattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kiṃ punarbhagavan bodhisattvā ito buddhakṣetrātpariniṣpannā anyeṣāṃ vā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmantikātsukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante? bhagavānāha - ito hyajita buddhakṣetrād dvāsaptatikoṭīniyutāni bodhisattvānāṃ pariniṣpannāni yāni sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante pariniṣpannānāmavaivartikānāṃ bahubuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyavaropitaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ, kaḥ punarvādastataḥ parīttataraiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ duṣprasahasya tathāgatasyāntikādaṣṭādaśakoṭīniyutaśatāni bodhisattvānāṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | pūrvāntare digbhāge ratnākaro nāma tathāgato viharati | tasyāntikānnavatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | jyotiṣprabhasya tathāgatasyāntikāddvāviṃśatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | amitaprabhasya tathāgatasyāntikātpañcaviṃśatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | lokapradīpasya tathāgatasyāntikātṣaṣṭibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | nāgābhibhuvastathāgatasyāntikāccatuḥṣaṣṭirbodhisattvakoṭyaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | virajaḥprabhasya tathāgatasyāntikātpañcaviṃśatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | siṃhasya tathāgatasyāntikātṣoḍaśabodhisattvakoṭyaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | siṃhasya tathāgatasyāntikādaṣṭādaśabodhisattvasahasrāni sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatasyante | śrīkūṭasya tathāgatasyāntikādekāśītibodhisattvakoṭīniyutāni sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | narendrarājasya tathāgatasyāntikāddaśabodhisattvakoṭīniyutāni sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | balābhijñasya tathāgatasyāntikāddvādaśabodhisattvasahasrāṇi sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyante | puṣpadhvajasya (

children.translated_text: ) from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained vigor, proceeding on a single journey, having left behind ninety <s>kalpa-koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands in the course of a single eight-day period, will be born in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. From the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jvalanādhipati</s>, twelve <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be born in <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. From the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vaiśāradyaprāpta</s>, sixty-nine <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be born in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> in order to see, worship, attend upon, and question the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>. By this method, <s>Ajita</s>, even if I were to recite the names of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> for a full <s>koṭi-niyuta</s> of <s>kalpas</s>—those from whose presence <s>bodhisattvas</s> come to the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> to see, worship, and attend upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>—it would not be possible to reach the end. [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> 42]

When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ajita</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Will <s>bodhisattvas</s>, Blessed One, who have matured from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> or from the presence of other <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, be born in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>?' The Blessed One replied: 'From this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, seventy-two <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of matured <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be born in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>—irreversible ones who have planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>—not to mention those with lesser roots of merit. From the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Duṣprasaha</s>, eighteen <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundreds of <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be born in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. In the eastern direction, from the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnākara</s>, ninety <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be born in <s>Sukhāvatī</s>.
