children.text: paśya ajita kiyatsulabdhalābhāste sattvā ye 'mitābhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya nāmadheyaṃ śroṣyanti | nāpi te sattvā hīnādhimuktikā bhaviṣyanti ye 'ntaśaekacittaprasādamapi tasmiṃstathāgate 'bhilapyante, asmiṃśca dharmaparyāye | tasmāttarhi ajita ārocayāmi vaḥ, prativedayāmi sadevakasya lokasya purato 'sya dharmaparyāyasya śrāvaṇāya | trisāhasramahāsāhasramapi lokadhātumagnipūrṇamavagāhya atikramaikacittotpādamapi pratisāro na kartavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? bodhisattvakoṭyo hyajita aśravaṇādeṣāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ dharmaparyāyāṇāṃ vivartante 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ | tasmādasya dharmaparyāyasyādhyāśayena śravaṇodgrahaṇadhāraṇārthaṃ paryāvāptaye vistareṇa saṃprakāśāya bhāvanārthaṃ ca sumahadvīryamārabdhavyam | antaśa ekarātriṃdinamapi, ekagodohamātramapi, antaśaḥ pustakāvaropitaṃ kṛtvā sulikhito dhārayitavyaḥ | śāstṛsaṃjñā ca tatropādhyāye kartavyā ya icchati kṣipramaparimitān sattvānavaivartikatve 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ pratiṣṭhāpayitum, tacca tasya bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetraṃ draṣṭum, ātmanaśca viśiṣṭāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhasaṃpadaṃ parigrahītumiti | api tu khalu ajita atyarthaṃ sulabdhalābhāste sattvā avaropitakuśalamūlāḥ pūrvajinakṛtādhikārā buddhādhiṣṭhitāśca bhaviṣyanti, yeṣāmanāgate 'dhvani yāvatsaddharmavipralope vartamāne ime evaṃrūpā udārā dharmaparyāyāḥ sarvabuddhasaṃvarṇitāḥ sarvabuddhapraśastāḥ sarvabuddhānujñātā mahataḥ sarvajñajñānasya kṣipramāhārakāḥ śrotrāvabhāsamāgamiṣyanti | ye śrutvā codāraprītiprāmodyaṃ pratilapsyanta udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti parebhyo vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, bhāvanābhiratāśca bhaviṣyanti, antaśo likhitvā pūjayiṣyanti, bahu ca te puṇyaṃ prasaviṣyanti, yasya na sukarā saṃkhyā kartum | iti hi ajita yattathāgatena kartavyam, kṛtaṃ mayā | yuṣmābhiridānīṃ nirvicikitsāyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | mā saṃśayata asaṅgamanāvaraṇaṃ buddhajñānam | mā bhūtsarvākārāvaropitaratnamaye bandhanāgāre praveśaḥ | durlabho hi ajita buddhotpādaḥ | durlabhā dharmadeśanā | durlabhā kṣaṇasaṃpat | ākhyātā ca ajita mayā sarvakuśalamūlapāramitāprāptiḥ | yūyamidānīmabhiyujyata pratipadyadhvam | asya khalu punarajita dharmaparyāyasya mahatīṃ parīndanāṃ karomi | avipraṇāśāya buddhadharmāṇāmanantardhānāya parākramiṣyatha | mā tathāgatājñāṃ kṣobhayiṣyatha || Sukhv_43 ||
children.translated_text: See, <s>Ajita</s>, how fortunate are those beings who will hear the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One! Nor will those beings be of inferior aspiration who produce even a single moment of faith in that <s>Tathāgata</s> and in this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma). Therefore, <s>Ajita</s>, I declare and proclaim this before the world together with its gods, for the hearing of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. Even if one must plunge through a <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (great trichiliocosm) world-realm filled with fire, one should not give rise to regret for even a single moment of faith. Why? Because, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> fall away from unsurpassed perfect <s>bodhi</s> through not hearing such <s>dharmaparyāyas</s> as this. Therefore, great effort should be made with earnest aspiration for hearing, grasping, retaining, comprehending, and extensively illuminating this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, and for its cultivation. Even for a single day and night, even for the duration of a single cow-milking, and at the very least, having written it in a book, one should preserve it well. And the teacher from whom one receives it should be regarded as one's master, if one wishes to quickly establish innumerable beings in the irreversibility of unsurpassed perfect <s>bodhi</s>, and to see that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the Blessed One <s>Amitābha</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and to obtain for oneself the splendid attainment of the array of qualities adorning the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. Moreover, <s>Ajita</s>, those beings will be supremely fortunate who have planted roots of merit, who have performed meritorious deeds under former <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), and who will be sustained by the <s>Buddhas</s>—those who in the future, when the true <s>Dharma</s> is disappearing, will hear such noble <s>dharmaparyāyas</s> as this, praised by all <s>Buddhas</s>, commended by all <s>Buddhas</s>, approved by all <s>Buddhas</s>, which quickly bring about the great omniscient knowledge. Those who, having heard, will obtain sublime joy and gladness, will grasp, retain, recite, and comprehend them, will extensively illuminate them for others, and will delight in their cultivation, and at the very least will copy and worship them—they will produce immense merit, the measure of which is not easy to calculate. Thus, <s>Ajita</s>, what was to be done by the <s>Tathāgata</s> has been done by me. Now you should practice the yoga of non-doubt. Do not harbor doubt—the <s>buddhajñāna</s> (Buddha-knowledge) is unobstructed and without barriers. Let there not be entry into the prison-house adorned with all manner of jewels, planted in every way. For rare, <s>Ajita</s>, is the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>. Rare is the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Rare is the attainment of a favorable opportunity. And I have declared, <s>Ajita</s>, the attainment of the perfection of all roots of merit. Now exert yourselves and practice! I make a great entrustment of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> to you. You should strive for the non-disappearance and non-vanishing of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. Do not transgress the command of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. [<s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> 43]

children.text: START Sukhv 44:
children.translated_text: [Section 44:]

children.text: Sukhv, Vaidya 252
atha khalu punarbhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
children.translated_text: Then at that time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke these verses:

children.text: na me akṛtapuṇyānāṃ śravā bheṣyanti īdṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those without merit will not hear such things as these;

children.text: ye tu te śūra siddhārthāḥ śroṣyanti ca imāṃ giram // Sukhv_vs_49 //
children.translated_text: But those heroes who have accomplished their aims will hear this speech. [Sukhv verse 49]

children.text: dṛṣṭo yaiśca hi saṃbuddho lokanāthaḥ prabhaṃkaraḥ //
children.translated_text: Those by whom the Perfectly Enlightened One, the Lord of the World, the Light-maker, has been seen,

children.text: sagauravaiḥ śruto dharmaḥ prītiṃ prāpsyanti te parām // Sukhv_vs_50 //
children.translated_text: And who have heard the <s>Dharma</s> with reverence — they shall attain supreme joy. [Sukhv verse 50]

children.text: na śakta hīnehi kusīdadṛṣṭibhiḥ buddhāna dharmeṣu prasāda vinditum /
children.translated_text: Those of low and lazy views are unable to find faith in the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: ye buddhakṣetreṣu akārṣi pūjāṃ trailokanāthāna caryāsu śikṣiṣu // Sukhv_vs_51 //
children.translated_text: Those who have made offerings in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) and trained in the conduct of the Lords of the Three Worlds. [Sukhv verse 51]

children.text: yathāndhakāre puruṣo hyacakṣuḥ mārgaṃ na jāne kutu saṃprakāśayet /
children.translated_text: Just as a blind man in darkness cannot know the path — how then could he illuminate it?

children.text: sarvaṃ tathā śrāvaka buddhajñāne ajānakāḥ kiṃ punaradya sattvāḥ // Sukhv_vs_52 //
children.translated_text: So too all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) are ignorant of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge — how much more so ordinary beings! [Sukhv verse 52]

children.text: buddho hi buddhasya guṇāṃ prajānate na devanāgāsurayakṣaśrāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Only a <s>Buddha</s> can know the virtues of a <s>Buddha</s> — not <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, or <s>śrāvakas</s>;

children.text: anekabuddhāna pi no gatī yatho buddhasya jñāne hi prakāśyamāne // Sukhv_vs_53 //
children.translated_text: Even the understanding of numerous <s>Buddhas</s> does not reach its limit, when the knowledge of a <s>Buddha</s> is being revealed. [Sukhv verse 53]

children.text: yadi sarvasattvāḥ samatā bhaveyuḥ viśuddhajñāne paramārthakovidāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if all beings were equal, skilled in the highest truth with purified knowledge,

children.text: te kalpakoṭīratha vāpi uttare naikasya buddhasya guṇān katheyuḥ // Sukhv_vs_54 //
children.translated_text: They could not describe the virtues of even one <s>Buddha</s> in <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> or even more. [Sukhv verse 54]

children.text: atrāntare nirvṛta te bhaveyuḥ prakāśamānā bahukalpakoṭīḥ /
children.translated_text: In the meanwhile they would pass into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, even while illuminating for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: na ca buddhajñānasya pramāṇu labhyate tathā hi jñānāścaryaṃ jinānām // Sukhv_vs_55 //
children.translated_text: No measure of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge can be found — such indeed is the wonder of the knowledge of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones). [Sukhv verse 55]

children.text: tasmānnaraḥ paṇḍita vijñajātiyaḥ yo mahya vākyamabhiśraddadheya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, let the wise person, born of good family, who would have faith in my words,

children.text: kṛtsnāṃ sa sākṣājjinajñānamārgān buddhaḥ prajānaṃ ti girāmudīrayet // Sukhv_vs_56 //
children.translated_text: Directly knowing all the paths of <s>Jina</s>-knowledge, as a <s>Buddha</s> who knows, utter this speech. [Sukhv verse 56]

children.text: kadāci labhyati manuṣyalābhaḥ kadāci buddhāna pi prādurbhāvaḥ /
Sukhv, Vaidya 253
śraddhārthaprajñā sucireṇa labhyate tasyārthaprāptyai janayet vīryam // Sukhv_vs_57 //
children.translated_text: Faith, purpose, and wisdom are attained only after a long time — one should generate <s>vīrya</s> (effort) for their attainment. [Sukhv verse 57]
Rare is the attainment of human birth; rare too is the appearance of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: ya īdṛśāṃ dharma śruṇitva śreṣṭhāṃ labhyanti prītiṃ sugataṃ smarantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, having heard such an excellent <s>Dharma</s>, attain joy while remembering the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One),

children.text: te mitramasmākamatītamadhvani ye cāpi bodhāya jananti chandam // Sukhv_vs_58 //
children.translated_text: They are our friends from the past journey, and they too generate the aspiration for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). [Sukhv verse 58]

children.text: iti || Sukhv_44 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends [Section 44]. [Sukhv 44]

children.text: START Sukhv 45:
children.translated_text: [Section 45:]

children.text: asmin khalu punardharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe dvādaśānāṃ sattvaniyutakoṭīnāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddham | caturviṃśatyā koṭiniyutaśataphalaṃ prāptam | aṣṭānāṃ bhikṣuśatānāmanupādāyāsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni | pañcaviṃśatyā bodhisattvakoṭībhiranutpattikadharmakṣāntiḥ pratilabdhā | devamānuṣikāyāśca prajāyāścatvāriṃśatkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāmanutpannapūrvāṇyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpannāni | sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapattaye ca kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasya darśanakāmatayā | sarve ca te tatropapadya anupūrveṇa mañjusvarā nāma tathāgatā anyeṣu lokadhātuṣūpapatsyante | aśītiśca niyutakoṭyo dīpaṃkare tathāgate labdhakṣāntikā avaivartikā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheramitāyuṣaiva tathāgatena paripācitāḥ pūrvabodhisattvacaryāṃ carantastāśca sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapadya pūrvapraṇidhānacaryāḥ paripūrayiṣyanti || Sukhv_45 ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, when this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (Dharma discourse) was being spoken, the pure <s>Dharma</s>-eye, free from dust and stain, was purified regarding the <s>dharmas</s> for twelve <s>niyuta</s>-<s>koṭīs</s> of beings. Twenty-four hundred <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> attained the fruit. The minds of eight hundred <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) were liberated from the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) without grasping. Twenty-five <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). And for forty <s>koṭī-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of the assembly of <s>devas</s> and humans, minds that had never before arisen were aroused toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening), and roots of merit were planted for rebirth in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, out of desire to see <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>. All of them, having been reborn there, will in due course become <s>Tathāgatas</s> named <s>Mañjusvara</s> (Sweet-Voiced) in other world-realms. And eighty <s>niyuta-koṭīs</s> who had attained patient acceptance under <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, irreversible from <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, having been brought to maturity by <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> himself, and practicing the former <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct — they too will be reborn in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> and will fulfill the practices of their former vows. [Sukhv 45]

children.text: START Sukhv 46:
children.translated_text: [Section 46:]

children.text: tasyāṃ velāyāmayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ ṣadvikāraṃ prākampat | vividhāni ca prātihāryāṇi saṃdṛśyante sma | pṛthivyāṃ saṃskṛtamabhūt | divyamānuṣyakāni ca tūryāṇi saṃpravāditānyabhūvan | anumodanāśabdena ca yāvadakaniṣṭhabhuvanaṃ vijñaptamabhūt || Sukhv_46 ||
children.translated_text: At that time, this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s> (great trichiliocosm) trembled in six ways, and various miracles were seen. The earth was adorned, and divine and human musical instruments sounded. The sound of rejoicing was proclaimed as far as the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven. [Sukhv 46]

children.text: START Sukhv 47:
children.translated_text: [Section 47:]

children.text: idamavocadbhagavānāttamanāḥ | ajito bodhisattvo mahāsattva āyuṣmāṃścānandaḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragaruḍagandharvasya loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti || Sukhv_47 ||
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, gratified. The <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> <s>Ajita</s> (Maitreya), the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, and that entire assembly, together with the world of <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words. [Sukhv 47]

children.text: bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasya sukhāvatīguṇavarṇaparikīrtanaṃ bodhisattvānāmavaivartyabhūmipraveśaḥ amitābhasya parivartaḥ sukhāvatīvyūho mahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: The proclamation of the virtues and qualities of the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> of <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>, the entry of <s>bodhisattvas</s> into the stage of non-retrogression, the chapter on <s>Amitābha</s> — the <s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s>, is complete.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat |
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that which is their cessation — thus speaks the Great Ascetic.
